sentences.zh: 王渾

translations.literal: Wang Hun.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun

sentences.zh: 王渾，字玄沖，太原晉陽人也。

translations.literal: Wang Hun, style Xuanzhong, was a man of Jinyang in Taiyuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun, courtesy name Xuanzhong, was a native of Jinyang in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 父昶，魏司空。

translations.literal: His father was Chang, Minister of Works of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Wang Chang, had served Wei as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 渾沈雅有器量。

translations.literal: Hun was deep and refined and had vessel-like capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun was grave, cultivated, and of generous measure.

sentences.zh: 襲父爵京陵侯，辟大將軍曹爽掾。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's noble rank as Marquis of Jingling and was summoned as an aide to General-in-chief Cao Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded to his father's title as Marquis of Jingling and joined the staff of General-in-chief Cao Shuang.

sentences.zh: 爽誅，隨例免。

translations.literal: Shuang was executed; he was dismissed following the precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Shuang was executed, Wang Hun lost his post like others swept up in the purge.

sentences.zh: 起為懷令，參文帝安東軍事，累遷散騎黃門侍郎、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was raised up as magistrate of Huai, participated in Prince Wen's Eastern Pacification military affairs, and by successive promotions became Gentleman for All-Purpose at the Yellow Gate and Regular Gentleman for All-Purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as magistrate of Huai, he served on the staff for Prince Wen's eastern command, then rose to gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gate and regular attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 咸熙中為越騎校尉。

translations.literal: In the Xianxi era he became Colonel of Yueqi Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianxi years he was appointed colonel of the élite Yue cavalry.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，加揚烈將軍，遷徐州刺史。

translations.literal: When Martial Emperor received the abdication, he was added General Who Spreads Fury and transferred to Governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne by abdication, Wang Hun was named General Who Spreads Might and inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時年荒歲饑，渾開倉振贍，百姓賴之。

translations.literal: At the time years were barren and harvests famine-stricken; Hun opened the granaries to relieve and succor; the common people relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Famine gripped the region; he opened government granaries for relief, and the people depended on him to survive.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，增封邑千八百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi, his fief households were increased by one thousand eight hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taishi his appanage was enlarged by eighteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷東中郎將，監淮北諸軍事，鎮許昌。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was transferred to General of the Gentlemen of the East, supervised all military affairs north of the Huai, and garrisoned Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted general of the eastern palace guard, put in charge of forces north of the Huai, and stationed at Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 數陳損益，多見納用。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he set forth what would detract or add benefit; much was accepted and employed.
translations.idiomatic: He often submitted practical recommendations, and the court adopted most of them.

sentences.zh: 轉征虜將軍、監豫州諸軍事、假節，領豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He was turned to General Who Conquers the Barbarians, supervised all military affairs of Yuzhou, granted credentials, and concurrently held Governor of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He became general who conquers foes, military overseer of Yuzhou with ceremonial baton, while serving as Yuzhou's regional inspector.

sentences.zh: 渾與吳接境，宣佈威信，前後降附甚多。

translations.literal: Hun bordered Wu, spread declaration of awe-inspiring trust, and before and after those who surrendered and attached were very many.
translations.idiomatic: His territory lay against Wu; he projected authority and good faith, and enemy soldiers defected to him in large numbers over time.

sentences.zh: 吳將薛瑩、魯淑眾號十萬，淑向弋陽，瑩向新息。

translations.literal: Wu generals Xue Ying and Lu Shu, their masses claiming one hundred thousand—Shu moved toward Yiyang, Ying toward Xinxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu commanders Xue Ying and Lu Shu led a host said to number one hundred thousand: Lu Shu drove on Yiyang, Xue Ying on Xinxi.

sentences.zh: 時州兵並放休息，眾裁一旅，浮淮潛濟，出其不意，瑩等不虞晉師之至。

translations.literal: At the time prefectural troops were altogether furloughed in rest; the mass was only one brigade; they floated the Huai and secretly crossed, coming out beyond their expectation; Ying and the rest did not anticipate the arrival of Jin's army.
translations.idiomatic: With provincial troops stood down and barely one brigade at hand, he crossed the Huai in secret and caught the enemy unprepared; Xue Ying had not expected Jin forces to appear.

sentences.zh: 渾擊破之，以功封次子尚為關內侯。

translations.literal: Hun struck and broke them; by merit he enfeoffed his second son Shang as Marquis Within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun shattered their army and, for this merit, had his second son Wang Shang enfeoffed as marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 遷安東將軍、都督揚州諸軍事，鎮壽春。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the East, commanded all military affairs of Yangzhou, and garrisoned Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general who pacifies the east and area commander for Yangzhou, with headquarters at Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 吳人大佃皖城，圖為邊害。

translations.literal: Wu people greatly cultivated field camps at Wancheng, plotting to become a border harm.
translations.idiomatic: Wu had developed a major military farm at Wancheng, intending to harass the frontier.

sentences.zh: 渾遣揚州刺史應綽督淮南諸軍攻破之，並破諸別屯，焚其積穀百八十餘萬斛、稻苗四千餘頃、船六百餘艘。

translations.literal: Hun dispatched Yangzhou Inspector Ying Chuo to supervise all Huainan armies, smash them, and together smash the various separate encampments, burning their accumulated grain of more than one million eight hundred thousand hu, rice seedlings of more than four thousand qing, and boats of more than six hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun sent Yangzhou's regional inspector Ying Chuo at the head of the Huainan armies to overrun the position, destroy satellite camps, and burn over 1.8 million hu of grain, more than four thousand qing of paddy, and upward of six hundred boats.

sentences.zh: 渾遂陳兵東疆，視其地形險易，曆觀敵城，察攻取之勢。

translations.literal: Hun thereupon arrayed troops on the eastern frontier, inspected the terrain's peril and ease, successively viewed enemy cities, and examined the momentum of attack and seizure.
translations.idiomatic: He then deployed along the eastern border, studied the ground, toured enemy towns, and assessed how an offensive might unfold.

sentences.zh: 及大舉伐吳，渾率師出橫江，遣參軍陳慎、都尉張喬攻尋陽瀨鄉，又擊吳牙門將孔忠，皆破之，獲吳將周興等五人。

translations.literal: When there was a great campaign to attack Wu, Hun led the army out from Hengjiang, dispatched aides Chen Shen and commandant Zhang Qiao to attack Xunyang's Laixiang, and again struck Wu's gate general Kong Zhong, all smashing them, capturing Wu generals Zhou Xing and five others.
translations.idiomatic: In the full-scale invasion of Wu, Wang Hun advanced from Hengjiang, sent staff officer Chen Shen and commandant Zhang Qiao against Laixiang in Xunyang, and also defeated Wu gate general Kong Zhong, taking five captives including commander Zhou Xing.

sentences.zh: 又遣殄吳護軍李純據高望城，討吳將俞恭，破之，多所斬獲。

translations.literal: Again he dispatched Exterminator-of-Wu Protector Li Chun to occupy Gaowang city, attacked Wu general Yu Gong, smashed him, and there were many beheadings and captures.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered protector Li Chun of the Wu-extermination force to seize Gaowang, where he routed Wu general Yu Gong with heavy casualties and prisoners.

sentences.zh: 吳曆武將軍陳代、平虜將軍硃明懼而來降。

translations.literal: The Wu generals Chen Dai, who held the rank of liwu jiangjun, and Zhu Ming, General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, fearing, came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wu commanders Chen Dai and Zhu Ming, unnerved by the Jin advance, crossed over and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 吳丞相張悌、大將軍孫震等率眾數萬指城陽，渾遣司馬孫疇、揚州刺史周浚擊破之，臨陣斬二將，及首虜七千八百級，吳人大震。

translations.literal: Wu Chancellor Zhang Ti, Great General Sun Zhen, and others led masses numbering several tens of thousands toward Chengyang; Hun dispatched Major Sun Chou and Yangzhou Inspector Zhou Jun to smash them, on the battlefield beheading the two generals, and heads and captives seven thousand eight hundred grades; Wu people were greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Zhang Ti and great general Sun Zhen of Wu marched tens of thousands toward Chengyang; Wang Hun sent major Sun Chou and inspector Zhou Jun to crush them, killing both commanders on the field and claiming 7,800 counted heads and prisoners, which stunned Wu.

sentences.zh: 孫皓司徒何植、建威將軍孫晏送印節詣渾降。

translations.literal: Sun Hao's Minister of Education He Zhi and General Who Establishes Might Sun Yan delivered seals and credentials to Hun to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao's minister He Zhi and general Sun Yan brought the seals of office to Wang Hun and capitulated.

sentences.zh: 既而王濬破石頭，降孫皓，威名益振。

translations.literal: Subsequently Wang Jun smashed Shitou, made Sun Hao submit, and awe-inspiring name increasingly shook.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wang Jun took Shitou and forced Sun Hao to yield, and his renown eclipsed others'.

sentences.zh: 明日，渾始濟江，登建鄴宮，釃酒高會。

translations.literal: The next day, Hun for the first time crossed the river, ascended the Jianye palace, sprinkled wine, and held a high feast.
translations.idiomatic: Only the next day did Wang Hun cross the Yangzi, enter the Jianye palace, and hold a lavish victory banquet.

sentences.zh: 自以先據江上，破皓中軍，案甲不進，致在王濬之後。

translations.literal: He himself thought he had first occupied the river's upper reaches, smashed Hao's central army, rested armor and did not advance, causing him to be after Wang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: He believed he had held the river line first and broken Sun Hao's main force, yet by holding back he let Wang Jun finish the conquest ahead of him.

sentences.zh: 意甚愧恨，有不平之色，頻奏濬罪狀，時人譏之。

translations.literal: His intent was very ashamed and resentful; he had an unlevel countenance; repeatedly he memorialized Jun's crimes and conditions; people of the time mocked him.
translations.idiomatic: Bitter and humiliated, he showed his pique and filed repeated charges against Wang Jun, for which contemporaries ridiculed him.

sentences.zh: 帝下詔曰：「使持節、都督揚州諸軍事、安東將軍、京陵侯王渾，督率所統，遂逼秣陵，令賊孫皓救死自衛，不得分兵上赴，以成西軍之功，又摧大敵，獲張悌，使皓途窮勢盡，面縛乞降。

translations.literal: The Emperor issued an edict saying: Bearer of credentials, commander of all military affairs of Yangzhou, General Who Pacifies the East, Marquis of Jingling Wang Hun, leading what he commanded, thereupon pressed Moling, making the bandit Sun Hao strive to save himself in self-defense, unable to divide troops to go up in aid, thereby completing the western army's merit, and again crushed a great foe, captured Zhang Ti, made Hao's road exhausted and power spent, bound face-forward and begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor proclaimed: Bearer of the baton and area commander for Yangzhou, General Who Pacifies the East, Marquis of Jingling Wang Hun pinned Moling so tightly that Sun Hao could only defend himself and could not shift troops upstream—thus clearing the way for the western column's success—while also shattering a major enemy force, capturing Zhang Ti, and driving Sun Hao to rope himself and offer surrender.

sentences.zh: 遂平定秣陵，功勳茂著。

translations.literal: Thereupon he pacified Moling; merit and achievement were luxuriantly manifest.
translations.idiomatic: In this way Moling was secured; his achievement stood out in full measure.

sentences.zh: 其增封八千戶，進爵為公，封子澄為亭侯、弟湛為關內侯，賜絹八千匹。

translations.literal: Increase his enfeoffment by eight thousand households; advance noble rank to duke; enfeoff son Cheng as village marquis, younger brother Zhan as Marquis Within the Passes; bestow eight thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: His fief rose by eight thousand households, his title advanced to duke, his son Wang Cheng made village marquis and his brother Wang Zhan marquis within the passes, with a gift of eight thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 」轉征東大將軍，復鎮壽陽。

translations.literal: He was turned to General Who Conquers the East and again garrisoned Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned general who conquers the east and returned to headquarters at Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 渾不尚刑名，處斷明允。

translations.literal: Hun did not esteem punishments and names; his dispositions were clear and fair.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun was no legalist pedant; his judgments were lucid and even-handed.

sentences.zh: 時吳人新附，頗懷畏懼。

translations.literal: At the time Wu people had newly attached and largely harbored fear.
translations.idiomatic: The newly submitted people of Wu were still anxious.

sentences.zh: 渾撫循羈旅，虛懷綏納，座無空席，門不停賓。

translations.literal: Hun comforted and followed the sojourners, emptied his bosom and peacefully received; seats had no empty mats; the gate did not stop guests.
translations.idiomatic: He put displaced gentry at ease, received them with open courtesy, kept every seat filled, and turned no caller from his door.

sentences.zh: 於是江東之士莫不悅附。

translations.literal: Thereupon gentlemen east of the river none did not joyfully attach.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangdong notables flocked to him willingly.

sentences.zh: 徵拜尚書左僕射，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Left Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, added Regular Cavalier Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as senior vice-president of the Secretariat and given the concurrent title of regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 會朝臣立議齊王攸當之籓，渾上書諫曰：「伏承聖詔，憲章古典，進齊王攸為上公，崇其禮儀，遣攸之國。

translations.literal: It happened that court ministers debated that Prince of Qi You ought to go to his fief; Hun submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying: Prostrate I receive the sagely edict, taking classical antiquity as model, advancing Prince of Qi You to senior duke, exalting his ritual and ceremony, dispatching You to his state.
translations.idiomatic: When ministers argued that Prince You of Qi must go to his princedom, Wang Hun memorialized in protest: I have heard Your Majesty's edict, framed on ancient precedent, raising Prince You of Qi to grand duke, honoring his rites, and sending him to his domain.

sentences.zh: 昔周氏建國，大封諸姬，以籓帝室，永世作憲。

translations.literal: In olden times the Zhou house established the state and greatly enfeoffed the various Ji, thereby to fence the imperial house, making eternal-age model.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founded their rule they invested many Ji kinsmen as bulwarks of the throne, a pattern meant to last for ages.

sentences.zh: 至於公旦，武王之弟，左右王事，輔濟大業，不使歸籓。

translations.literal: As for the Duke of Zhou, Martial King's younger brother, he assisted at the king's business and aided the great enterprise, and was not made to return to a fief.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou, brother to King Wu, stayed at court to govern and never was packed off to a distant fief.

sentences.zh: 明至親義著，不可遠朝故也。

translations.literal: It clarifies that utmost kinship and righteousness were manifest and could not be distanced from court for that reason.
translations.idiomatic: That shows how close kin whose virtue is plain must not be banished from the capital.

sentences.zh: 是故周公得以聖德光弼幼主，忠誠著于《金縢》，光述文武仁聖之德。

translations.literal: For this reason the Duke of Zhou was able with sagely virtue broadly to assist the young lord; loyalty and faithfulness were manifest in the 'Metal-bound Coffer'; he brightly transmitted Martial and Civil's benevolent sagely virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Duke of Zhou could guide the boy king with sage virtue; his loyalty shines in the Metal-bound Coffer ode, carrying forward the humane renown of Kings Wen and Wu.

sentences.zh: 攸于大晉，姬旦之親也。

translations.literal: You toward Great Jin is kin like Ji Dan.
translations.idiomatic: For Great Jin, Prince You stands in the same relation as the Duke of Zhou did to the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 宜贊皇朝，與聞政事，實為陛下腹心不貳之臣。

translations.literal: He ought to assist the imperial court, participate in hearing government affairs; in truth he is Your Majesty's belly-and-heart undivided minister.
translations.idiomatic: He should help govern at court and hear state business; he is in truth an intimate minister on whom Your Majesty can rely without reserve.

sentences.zh: 且攸為人，修潔義信，加以懿親，志存忠貞。

translations.literal: Moreover You as a person is cultivated, clean, righteous, and trustworthy; added to that are his excellent kinship ties; his intent rests in loyal faithfulness.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Prince You is scrupulous, upright, and trustworthy, and as imperial kin his loyalty is beyond question.

sentences.zh: 今陛下出攸之國，假以都督虛號，而無典戎幹方之實，去離天朝，不預王政。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty sends You out to his state, lending him the empty title of area commander yet without the reality of commanding troops and guarding a region; he departs and is separated from the heavenly court, not participating in royal government.
translations.idiomatic: To banish him to his fief with only a nominal area command—no real military authority—and cut him off from court and policy-making is another matter.

sentences.zh: 傷母弟至親之體，虧友于款篤之義，懼非陛下追述先帝、文明太后待攸之宿意也。

translations.literal: It injures the body of mother-and-younger-brother utmost kinship, diminishes the friendly fraternal generous righteousness; I fear it is not Your Majesty's intent to pursue and narrate the late Emperor and Civilized Bright Empress Dowager's long-standing intent toward You.
translations.idiomatic: It wounds the bond between mother and younger son and frays brotherly affection; I doubt it matches what the late emperor and Empress Dowager Wénmíng intended for Prince You.

sentences.zh: 若以攸望重，於事宜出者，今以汝南王亮代攸。

translations.literal: If because You is weighty in repute, in the affair it is fitting that he go out, now use Prince of Runan Liang in place of You.
translations.idiomatic: If senior standing truly requires someone to hold an external post, appoint Prince Liang of Runan in Prince You's stead.

sentences.zh: 亮，宣皇帝子，文皇帝弟，伷、駿各處方任，有內外之資，論以後慮，亦不為輕。

translations.literal: Liang is Exalted Emperor's son, Civil Emperor's younger brother; Zhou and Jun each occupy square duties, having inner and outer resources; judged by later worries, it is also not light.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liang is a son of Emperor Xuan and brother to Emperor Wen; princes Zhou and Jun already hold key posts inside and out, so the dynasty would still be well covered.

sentences.zh: 攸今之國，適足長異同之論，以損仁慈之美耳。

translations.literal: You now going to his state is only sufficient to lengthen dissident sameness discourse, thereby to harm benevolent and kind beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Sending Prince You away now would only fuel factional talk and tarnish Your Majesty's reputation for cherishing kin.

sentences.zh: 而令天下窺陛下有不崇親親之情，臣竊為陛下不取也。

translations.literal: And it would make the world peep that Your Majesty lacks the affection of honoring kin-as-kin; your servant privately holds that Your Majesty should not take this.
translations.idiomatic: It would suggest to the realm that you slight close family; I respectfully urge you not to do it.

sentences.zh: 若以妃後外親，任以朝政，則有王氏傾漢之權，呂產專朝之禍。

translations.literal: If because consorts and empresses' outer kin, entrusting them with court government, then there is Wang clan's power to overturn Han, Lü Chan's disaster of monopolizing court.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusting the consorts' affines with power invites a Wang Mang-style takeover or a Lü-clique stranglehold on government.

sentences.zh: 若以同姓至親，則有吳楚七國逆亂之殃。

translations.literal: If because same-surname utmost kin, then there is the misfortune of Wu and Chu seven states' rebellious disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Relying solely on imperial clansmen risks another revolt like the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu.

sentences.zh: 曆觀古今，苟事輕重，所在無不為害也。

translations.literal: Successively viewing ancient and present, wherever affairs' light and weight lay, there was none that did not become harm.
translations.idiomatic: History shows that every such expedient, whichever way the scales tilt, ends badly.

sentences.zh: 不可事事曲設疑防，慮方來之患者也。

translations.literal: One cannot in every matter bend to set suspicious defenses, considering coming troubles.
translations.idiomatic: You cannot hedge every policy against imaginary future threats.

sentences.zh: 唯當任正道而求忠良。

translations.literal: Only ought to entrust the correct way and seek loyal and good.
translations.idiomatic: The right course is to uphold proper principle and choose loyal, capable men.

sentences.zh: 若以智計猜物，雖親見疑，至於疏遠者亦何能自保乎！

translations.literal: If by schemes and calculations one suspects things, though kin are seen as suspect, as for the distant and estranged, how can they each preserve themselves!
translations.idiomatic: If you govern by suspicion, even kin become suspects, and those farther out cannot feel safe either.

sentences.zh: 人懷危懼，非為安之理。

translations.literal: People harboring peril and fear is not a pattern of peace.
translations.idiomatic: A court of frightened men is no recipe for stability.

sentences.zh: 此最有國有家者之深忌也。

translations.literal: This is what those who have state and family most deeply taboo.
translations.idiomatic: That is the gravest fear of any ruler with a realm to keep.

sentences.zh: 愚以為太子太保缺，宜留攸居之，與太尉汝南王亮、衛將軍楊珧共為保傅，幹理朝事。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly thinks the Grand Guardian to the Heir Apparent is vacant; it is fitting to retain You to dwell in it, together with Grand Commandant Prince of Runan Liang and Guards General Yang Yao jointly to be protectors and tutors, managing court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I suggest leaving the vacant post of heir-apparent grand guardian to Prince You, sharing guardianship of the heir with Grand Commandant Prince Liang of Runan and Guards General Yang Yao while they jointly administer court business.

sentences.zh: 三人齊位，足相持正，進有輔納廣義之益，退無偏重相傾之勢。

translations.literal: The three persons in aligned rank are sufficient mutually to uphold rectitude; advancing there is the benefit of assisting and receiving broad righteousness; retiring there is no situation of one-sided weight mutually tipping.
translations.idiomatic: The three would balance one another—cooperating for the heir's good without letting any one faction dominate.

sentences.zh: 令陛下有篤親親之恩，使攸蒙仁覆之惠。

translations.literal: Order Your Majesty to have generous honoring-kin intent, make You receive benevolent covering's favor.
translations.idiomatic: You would show true affection for kin while Prince You enjoys your protecting favor.

sentences.zh: 臣同國休戚，義在盡言，心之所見，不能默已。

translations.literal: Your servant shares the state's weal and woe; righteousness lies in exhausting speech; what the heart sees, cannot be silent.
translations.idiomatic: As I share the dynasty's fortunes, duty compels me to speak my mind; I cannot hold my tongue.

sentences.zh: 私慕魯女存國之志，敢陳愚見，觸犯天威。

translations.literal: Privately I admire the Lu woman's intent to preserve the state; I dare set forth foolish views, offending heavenly might.
translations.idiomatic: Like the woman of Lu who spoke to save her state, I risk your displeasure by offering these blunt views.

sentences.zh: 欲陛下事每盡善，冀萬分之助。

translations.literal: Desiring Your Majesty's affairs each to reach complete goodness, hoping for assistance of one ten-thousandth part.
translations.idiomatic: I wish every decision of yours to be sound and hope this may help in however small a measure.

sentences.zh: 臣而不言，誰當言者。

translations.literal: If your servant yet does not speak, who ought to speak.
translations.idiomatic: If I stay silent, who will tell you the truth?

sentences.zh: 」帝不納。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejected his advice.

sentences.zh: 太熙初，遷司徒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taixi, he was transferred to Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taixi he was appointed minister of education.

sentences.zh: 惠帝即位，加侍中，又京陵置士官，如睢陵比。

translations.literal: When Hui Emperor ascended the throne, he was added Palace Attendant, and again at Jingling official soldiers were established, comparable to Suiling.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Hui he gained the concurrent title of palace attendant, and a corps of household guards was authorized for the Jingling marquisate on the Suiling model.

sentences.zh: 及誅楊駿，崇重舊臣，乃加渾兵。

translations.literal: When it came to executing Yang Jun, honoring and weighting old ministers, thereupon Hun was added troops.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Jun's execution, as the court elevated senior officials, Wang Hun was granted a military guard.

sentences.zh: 渾以司徒文官，主史不持兵，持兵乃吏屬絳衣。

translations.literal: Hun, because the Minister of Education was a civil official, the chief clerk did not bear arms; bearing arms was then subordinate clerks' crimson robes.
translations.idiomatic: As minister of education—a civil post—his chief clerk had not carried arms; armed attendants had been the business of crimson-robed staff.

sentences.zh: 自以偶因時寵，權得持兵，非是舊典，皆令皁服。

translations.literal: He himself thought it was a chance because of the times' favor, by authority obtaining to bear arms, not being the old norm; he ordered all to wear black robes.
translations.idiomatic: He considered his armed escort a temporary favor, not precedent, and had the guards dress in black like ordinary household troops.

sentences.zh: 論者美其謙而識體。

translations.literal: Discussers praised his modesty and knowledge of forms.
translations.idiomatic: Observers commended his humility and sense of propriety.

sentences.zh: 楚王瑋將害汝南王亮等也。

translations.literal: Prince of Chu Wei was about to harm Prince of Runan Liang and others.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei of Chu was plotting to kill Prince Liang of Runan and his allies.

sentences.zh: 公孫宏說瑋曰：「昔宣帝廢曹爽，引太尉蔣濟參乘，以增威重。

translations.literal: Gongsun Hong persuaded Wei, saying: In olden times Exalted Emperor abolished Cao Shuang, led Grand Commandant Jiang Ji in the same carriage, thereby to increase awe-inspiring weight.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Hong urged him: When Emperor Xuan eliminated Cao Shuang, he had Grand Commandant Jiang Ji ride in his carriage to lend the coup solemn weight.

sentences.zh: 大王今舉非常事，宜得宿望，鎮厭眾心。

translations.literal: Great King now raises an extraordinary affair; it is fitting to obtain long-standing repute, suppressing and filling the multitude's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness is staging a coup; you need a figure of established prestige at your side to steady public opinion.

sentences.zh: 司徒王渾宿有威名，為三軍所信服，可請同乘，使物情有憑也。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Wang Hun long has awe-inspiring name; he is what the three armies trust and submit to; it is possible to request him to ride together, making things' feelings have a reliance.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wang Hun's name carries authority; the troops trust him—invite him into your carriage so the act looks legitimate.

sentences.zh: 」瑋從之。

translations.literal: Wei followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei agreed.

sentences.zh: 渾辭疾歸第，以家兵千餘人閉門距瑋。

translations.literal: Hun declined illness and returned to his residence, using household troops of more than one thousand men to shut the gate and resist Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun pleaded illness, went home, and barred his gates with over a thousand family retainers against the prince.

sentences.zh: 瑋不敢逼。

translations.literal: Wei did not dare press.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei did not dare force an entry.

sentences.zh: 俄而瑋以矯詔伏誅，渾乃率兵赴官。

translations.literal: Before long Wei because of forged edict was executed by law; Hun thereupon led troops to go to office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Prince Wei was executed for forging an edict, and Wang Hun then marched his guard to resume his duties.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗訪渾元會問郡國計吏方俗之宜，渾奏曰：「陛下欽明聖哲，光於遠近，明詔沖虛，詢及芻蕘，斯乃周文疇咨之求，仲尼不恥下問也。

translations.literal: The Emperor once consulted Hun at the Yuanhui about commandery and state accounting clerks' local customs' appropriateness; Hun memorialized, saying: Your Majesty is reverent, bright, sagely and wise, your light reaches far and near; the bright edict is empty and humble, inquiring reaching to fodder and firewood; this is Zhou Wen's seeking counsel in fields, Confucius' not shaming to ask below.
translations.idiomatic: Once at the New Year audience the emperor asked Wang Hun how to question the regional clerks about local conditions. Wang Hun replied: Your sagely brilliance reaches everywhere; your modest edict consults even the humblest—like King Wen seeking advice in the fields or Confucius unashamed to learn from inferiors.

sentences.zh: 舊三朝元會前計吏詣軒下，侍中讀詔，計吏跪受。

translations.literal: By old rule, before the three courts' Yuanhui, accounting clerks went beneath the balustrade; the palace attendant read the edict; the accounting clerk knelt and received.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, before the triple audience at New Year, clerks stood below the gallery while an attendant read the formulaic rescript and each clerk knelt to receive it.

sentences.zh: 臣以詔文相承已久，無他新聲，非陛下留心方國之意也。

translations.literal: Your servant considers the edict's text mutually inherited already long, without other new sound; it is not Your Majesty's intent to take heart in the regions.
translations.idiomatic: That rote wording has been handed down for ages; it does not show Your Majesty's real interest in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 可令中書指宣明詔，問方土異同，賢才秀異，風俗好尚，農桑本務，刑獄得無冤濫，守長得無侵虐。

translations.literal: It is possible to order the Palace Secretariat to point and proclaim the bright edict, asking about regional soil's sameness and difference, worthy talents' excellence and difference, customs' likes and upholdings, agriculture and mulberry's root tasks, whether punishments and prisons obtain without wrongful excess, whether guardians and elders obtain without encroachment and tyranny.
translations.idiomatic: Have the Secretariat publish a clear instruction: ask about local conditions, notable talent, popular customs, farming and sericulture, miscarriages of justice, and oppressive magistrates.

sentences.zh: 其勤心政化興利除害者，授以紙筆，盡意陳聞。

translations.literal: Those who diligently take heart in government transformation, raising benefit and removing harm, grant paper and brush, exhaust intent and set forth hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Give paper and ink to those eager to report what helps or harms good government and let them write everything out.

sentences.zh: 以明聖指垂心四遠，不復因循常辭。

translations.literal: Thereby to clarify the sage finger hanging heart to the four far reaches, no longer following along common phrases.
translations.idiomatic: That would show the throne's concern for the four quarters instead of recycling empty phrases.

sentences.zh: 且察其答對文義，以觀計吏人才之實。

translations.literal: Moreover inspect their answer-reply's literary meaning, thereby to observe accounting clerks' human talent's substance.
translations.idiomatic: You can also judge the clerks' quality from the sense of their written answers.

sentences.zh: 又先帝時，正會後東堂見征鎮長史司馬、諸王國卿、諸州別駕。

translations.literal: Moreover under the late Emperor, after the proper meeting, the eastern hall saw expedition and garrison senior clerks and majors, various princely states' ministers, various prefectures' separate chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Under the late emperor, after the main audience, clerks from commands and garrisons, princely ministers, and prefectural deputies were received in the eastern hall.

sentences.zh: 今若不能別見，可前詣軒下，使侍中宣問，以審察方國，於事為便。

translations.literal: Now if it is not possible separately to meet, it is possible beforehand to go beneath the balustrade, order the palace attendant to proclaim and ask, thereby carefully to inspect the regions; toward affairs it is convenient.
translations.idiomatic: If private audiences are impractical, bring them below the gallery beforehand and let an attendant put your questions—an efficient way to learn about the localities.

sentences.zh: 」帝然之。

translations.literal: The Emperor deemed it so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 又詔渾錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Again he edicted Hun to record Masters of Writing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Wang Hun to serve as recording secretary for the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 渾所曆之職，前後著稱，及居台輔，聲望日減。

translations.literal: In the offices Hun passed through, before and after he was celebrated; when he dwelt at the terrace and carriage-strap, reputation and name daily diminished.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun had won praise in every post he held, but once he reached the highest councils his standing steadily declined.

sentences.zh: 薨，時年七十五，諡曰元。

translations.literal: He died; at the time age seventy-five; posthumous name was Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-five and received the posthumous epithet Yuan.

sentences.zh: 長子尚早亡，次子濟嗣。

translations.literal: The eldest son Shang died early; the second son Ji inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His firstborn, Wang Shang, had died young; the succession passed to his second son, Wang Ji.

translations.literal: The source text here is a lone equals sign, a typographical placeholder in the edition, not part of the narrative.

sentences.zh: 子濟

translations.literal: His son, Wang Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji

sentences.zh: =濟字武子。

translations.literal: A leading “=” (source artifact); Ji’s courtesy name was Wuzi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji, courtesy name Wuzi.

sentences.zh: 少有逸才，風姿英爽，氣蓋一時，好弓馬，勇力絕人，善《易》及《莊》、《老》，文詞俊茂，伎藝過人，有名當世，與姊夫和嶠及裴楷齊名。

translations.literal: In youth he had outstanding talent; his mien was bright and spirited, his air overshadowed the age; he loved bow and horse, his courage and strength cut off others; he was good at the *Changes* and at the *Zhuangzi* and *Laozi*; his literary phrasing was handsome and luxuriant, his arts and skills passed others; he had a name in the age, and with his elder sisters’ husband He Qiao and Pei Kai he had equal fame.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a youth he displayed rare ability—carriage keen and commanding, a presence that outshone his contemporaries. He delighted in archery and riding and surpassed others in bold strength. He was versed in the *Changes*, the *Zhuangzi*, and the *Laozi*; his prose was brilliant, his accomplishments exceptional. He ranked among the celebrated men of the day alongside his brother-in-law He Qiao and Pei Kai.

sentences.zh: 尚常山公主。

translations.literal: He was married to the Princess of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: He took the Princess of Changshan as his wife.

sentences.zh: 年二十，起家拜中書郎，以母憂去官。

translations.literal: At age twenty he first rose from home and was appointed Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat; on account of mourning for his mother he left office.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he entered service as a Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat, then resigned to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 起為驍騎將軍，累遷侍中，與侍中孔恂、王恂、楊濟同列，為一時秀彥。

translations.literal: He rose to be General of Agile Cavalry, and by successive transfers became Palace Attendant, standing in the same rank as Palace Attendants Kong Xun, Wang Xun, and Yang Ji, as outstanding talents of the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as General of Agile Cavalry, he rose through several posts to Palace Attendant, serving alongside Kong Xun, Wang Xun, and Yang Ji as one of the day’s most distinguished officials.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘗會公卿籓牧於式乾殿，顧濟、恂而謂諸公曰：「朕左右可謂恂恂濟濟矣！

translations.literal: The Martial Emperor once assembled the dukes, ministers, and frontier shepherds in the Shiqian Hall, looked toward Ji and Xun and said to the assembled lords: “Those at my left and right may be called xunxun and jiji!”
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu once gathered high ministers and regional governors in Shiqian Hall, glanced at Wang Ji and Kong Xun, and told the company, “The men at my side are truly orderly and abounding in talent.”

sentences.zh: 」每侍見，未嘗不諮論人物及萬機得失。

translations.literal: Each time he attended in service, there was never a time when he did not consult on persons and on the gains and losses of the myriad tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he attended the throne, he invariably joined in weighing character and the merits or faults of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 濟善於清言，修飾辭令，諷議將順，朝臣莫能尚焉。

translations.literal: Ji was good at pure talk, polished his phrases and commands, and in remonstrance and discussion inclined to compliance; no court minister could surpass him therein.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji excelled at *qingtan* discourse, shaped his speech with care, and framed advice so as to follow the emperor’s bent—none at court could match him in that art.

sentences.zh: 帝益親貴之。

translations.literal: The emperor increasingly drew him close and honored him.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign came to favor and esteem him all the more.

sentences.zh: 仕進雖速，論者不以主婿之故，咸謂才能致之。

translations.literal: Although his advancement in office was rapid, critics did not, because he was the emperor’s son-in-law, all say that it was by talent that he attained it.
translations.idiomatic: Though his career rose swiftly, observers attributed his success to ability rather than merely to his status as imperial son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 然外雖弘雅，而內多忌刻，好以言傷物，儕類以此少之。

translations.literal: Yet outwardly though he was broad and refined, inwardly he was much jealous and harsh, and liked to wound things with words; his peers for this thought less of him.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly magnanimous and cultivated, he was inwardly suspicious and cutting, prone to barbed remarks; contemporaries held him somewhat the less for it.

sentences.zh: 以其父之故，每排王濬，時議譏焉。

translations.literal: Because of the matter of his father, he repeatedly obstructed Wang Jun; contemporary opinion ridiculed him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Owing to his father’s quarrel with Wang Jun, he repeatedly worked against Jun, and opinion at court mocked him for it.

sentences.zh: 齊王攸當之籓，濟既陳請，又累使公主與甄德妻長廣公主俱入，稽顙泣請帝留攸。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qi, You, was about to go out to his fief, Ji had already presented remonstrance, and also repeatedly sent the princess together with Zhen De’s wife, the Princess of Changuang, both to enter, bow their foreheads to the ground, weep, and beg the emperor to retain You.
translations.idiomatic: As Prince Sima You of Qi prepared to depart for his princedom, Wang Ji had already petitioned against it; he also had the princess join Zhen De’s wife, the Princess of Changuang, in entering the palace, prostrating themselves in tears to beg the emperor to keep You at court.

sentences.zh: 帝怒謂侍中王戎曰：「兄弟至親，今出齊王，自是朕家事，而甄德、王濟連遣婦來生哭人！

translations.literal: The emperor angrily said to Palace Attendant Wang Rong: “Brothers are utmost kin; now sending out the Prince of Qi is naturally my household affair—yet Zhen De and Wang Ji in succession send their wives to come weep at a person alive!”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor angrily told Palace Attendant Wang Rong, “Brothers are my closest kin. Sending the Prince of Qi away is my own family matter—yet Zhen De and Wang Ji keep dispatching their wives to wail at me as if I were dead!”

sentences.zh: 」以忤旨，左遷國子祭酒，常侍如故。

translations.literal: For having offended the imperial intent, he was shifted left to be Libationer of the National University, his regular attendant status remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: For this breach of imperial will he was demoted to Libationer of the Imperial Academy while retaining his standing as a regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 數年，入為侍中。

translations.literal: After several years he entered [the capital] and became Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was recalled as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 時渾為僕射，主者處事或不當，濟性峻厲，明法繩之。

translations.literal: At the time Hun was Director of the Secretariat; the clerks in charge sometimes handled matters improperly; Ji’s nature was stern and severe, and he clarified the law and bound them with it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun then headed the Secretariat; when subordinates mishandled business, Wang Ji—by nature strict—insisted on clear application of statute.

sentences.zh: 素與從兄佑不平，佑黨頗謂濟不能顧其父，由是長同異之言。

translations.literal: He had long been at odds with his elder male cousin You; You’s faction largely said that Ji could not show regard for his father, and from this grew prolonged talk of agreement and disagreement.
translations.idiomatic: He had never been on good terms with his cousin Wang You; You’s partisans claimed Wang Ji failed in filial duty toward his father, and partisan whispers of division persisted.

sentences.zh: 出為河南尹，未拜，坐鞭王官吏免官。

translations.literal: He went out to be Governor of Henan; before he received appointment, he sat because of flogging Wang’s officials and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Governor of Henan but, before taking up the post, was stripped of rank for having had a Wang-clan official flogged.

sentences.zh: 而王佑始見委任。

translations.literal: And Wang You began to be entrusted and employed.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Wang You began to win the court’s trust and real authority.

sentences.zh: 而濟遂被斥外，於是乃移第北芒山下。

translations.literal: But Ji thereupon was cast out to the periphery, and at this then moved his residence beneath Mount Mang north [of Luoyang].
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji, relegated to the margins, thereupon relocated his household to the northern foot of Mount Mang.

sentences.zh: 性豪侈，麗服玉食。

translations.literal: By nature he was extravagant and luxurious, with splendid garments and jade[-like] food.
translations.idiomatic: He lived ostentatiously, draped in finery and dining with the costliest fare.

sentences.zh: 時洛京地甚貴，濟買地為馬埒，編錢滿之，時人謂為「金溝」。

translations.literal: At the time land in the capital of Luoyang was very expensive; Ji bought land to make a horse course, and strung it full of cash; people of the time called it the “gold ditch.”
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang real estate being exorbitant, he purchased a tract for a riding ring and paved it with strung cash—contemporaries dubbed it the “golden ditch.”

sentences.zh: 王愷以帝舅奢豪，有牛名「八百里駁」，常瑩其蹄角。

translations.literal: Wang Kai, because he was the emperor’s maternal uncle, was extravagant and proud; he had an ox named “Eight-hundred-li Piebald,” and constantly polished its hooves and horns.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kai, the emperor’s uncle by marriage, rivaled others in lavish display; he owned a famous ox called “Eight-hundred-*li* Piebald” and kept its hooves and horns burnished.

sentences.zh: 濟請以錢千萬與牛對射而賭之。

translations.literal: Ji requested to stake ten million cash against the ox in opposed archery and wager on it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji offered ten million cash in a shooting match against the beast, winner take all.

sentences.zh: 愷亦自恃其能，令濟先射。

translations.literal: Kai also trusted in his own ability, and ordered Ji to shoot first.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in his own skill, Wang Kai had Wang Ji shoot first.

sentences.zh: 一發破的，因據胡床，叱左右速探牛心來，須臾而至，一割便去。

translations.literal: One shot broke the target; thereupon he leaned on a folding stool, shouted to left and right to quickly fetch the ox’s heart; in a moment it arrived, one slice and he left.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji shattered the target with his first arrow, then lounged on a camp stool and barked at attendants to bring the ox’s heart; moments later it was served—one cut and he was done.

sentences.zh: 和嶠性至儉，家有好李，帝求之，不過數十。

translations.literal: He Qiao by nature was utmost frugal; his household had fine plums; the emperor sought them, and he gave no more than several tens.
translations.idiomatic: He Qiao was famously stingy; though his garden yielded superb plums, he parted with only a few dozen when the emperor asked.

sentences.zh: 濟候其上直，率少年詣園，共啖畢，伐樹而去。

translations.literal: Ji waited until he went up on duty, led youths to the garden, together ate them all, cut down the trees and left.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji waited until He Qiao was on palace duty, then led a band of young men to the orchard, devoured every plum, and felled the trees on leaving.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗幸其宅，供饌甚豐，悉貯琉璃器中。

translations.literal: The emperor once visited his house; the provisions for the feast were very abundant, all stored in glass vessels.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor once called at his home, the banquet was lavish, every dish presented in lustrous glassware.

sentences.zh: 蒸肫甚美，帝問其故，答曰：「以人乳蒸之。

translations.literal: The steamed pig’s trotter was very fine; the emperor asked the reason; he answered: “It was steamed with human milk.”
translations.idiomatic: The steamed trotters were exquisite; asked his secret, Wang Ji replied that he had steamed them in human milk.

sentences.zh: 」帝色甚不平，食未畢而去。

translations.literal: The emperor’s color was very unequal; before the food was finished he left.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign’s expression darkened; he rose and left before the meal ended.

sentences.zh: 濟善解馬性，嘗乘一馬，著連乾鄣泥，前有水，終不肯渡。

translations.literal: Ji was good at understanding horses’ natures; he once rode a horse, wearing linked-dry [pattern] mud-guards; ahead there was water; in the end it would not ford.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji read horses well. Riding one day in ornate mud-flaps, he found the animal would not cross a stream ahead.

sentences.zh: 濟云：「此必是惜鄣泥。

translations.literal: Ji said: “This must be cherishing the mud-guards.”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji said, “It must be sparing those flaps.”

sentences.zh: 」使人解去，便渡。

translations.literal: He had people remove them, and then it forded.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants removed them, and the horse crossed at once.

sentences.zh: 故杜預謂濟有馬癖。

translations.literal: Therefore Du Yu said Ji had a horse obsession.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Du Yu remarked that Wang Ji had a horse fetish.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗謂和嶠曰：「我將罵濟而後官爵之，何如？

translations.literal: The emperor once said to He Qiao: “I will curse Ji and afterward ennoble him with office—how would that be?”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked He Qiao, “Suppose I berate Wang Ji and then reward him with rank—what do you think?”

sentences.zh: 」嶠曰：「濟俊爽，恐不可屈。

translations.literal: Qiao said: “Ji is handsome and bright; I fear he cannot be bent.”
translations.idiomatic: He Qiao replied, “Wang Ji is proud and forthright; he will not easily bend.”

sentences.zh: 」帝因召濟，切讓之，既而曰：「知愧不？

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon summoned Ji, sharply reproved him, and afterward said: “Do you know shame?”
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign summoned Wang Ji, scolded him harshly, then asked, “Do you feel any shame?”

sentences.zh: 」濟答曰：「尺布鬥粟之謠，常為陛下恥之。

translations.literal: Ji answered: The ballad of a foot of cloth and a peck of grain—I constantly am ashamed for Your Majesty on its account.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji said the old verse about a foot of cloth and a peck of grain had long shamed him on the emperor’s behalf.

sentences.zh: 他人能令親疏，臣不能使親親，以此愧陛下耳。

translations.literal: Other men can make kin distant or close; your servant cannot make kin kin—on this I am ashamed before Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Others might pit kin against kin; he could not keep the emperor’s own brothers united—that was his shame toward the throne.

sentences.zh: 」帝默然。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗與濟弈棋，而孫皓在側，謂皓曰：「何以好剝人面皮？

translations.literal: The emperor once played weiqi with Ji, while Sun Hao was at the side; he said to Hao: “Why do you like to peel people’s facial skin?”
translations.idiomatic: Once, as Emperor Wu played chess with Wang Ji while Sun Hao stood by, he asked Sun Hao, “Why were you so fond of flaying men’s faces?”

sentences.zh: 」皓曰：「見無禮於君者則剝之。

translations.literal: Hao said: “When I saw one lacking in ritual toward the ruler, then I peeled him.”
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao replied, “I flayed those who showed disrespect to their lord.”

sentences.zh: 」濟時伸腳局下，而皓譏焉。

translations.literal: At the time Ji stretched his feet beneath the board, and Hao ridiculed him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji had stretched his legs under the board; Sun Hao used that to mock him.

sentences.zh: 尋使白衣領太僕。

translations.literal: Soon he was made to lead the Grand Coachman in white garb.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was ordered to oversee the Grand Coachman while still in undressed mourning white.

sentences.zh: 年四十六，先渾卒，追贈驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: At age forty-six he died before Hun; posthumously he was awarded General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-six, predeceasing Wang Hun, and was posthumously honored as General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 及其將葬，時賢無不畢至。

translations.literal: When it came to his being buried, worthies of the time none failed to arrive in full.
translations.idiomatic: At his funeral every notable of the day turned out.

sentences.zh: 孫楚雅敬濟，而後來，哭之甚悲，賓客莫不垂涕。

translations.literal: Sun Chu by refined respect honored Ji, but came late; he wept for him very sorrowfully; guests none failed to let fall tears.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chu, who deeply admired Wang Ji, arrived late yet wept with such grief that every mourner wept with him.

sentences.zh: 哭畢，向靈床曰：「卿常好我作驢鳴，我為卿作之。

translations.literal: When he finished weeping, he turned toward the spirit couch and said: “You always liked me to make a donkey’s bray; I will make one for you.”
translations.idiomatic: When he had done weeping, he addressed the bier: “You always wanted me to bray like a donkey—here it is for you.”

sentences.zh: 」體似聲真，賓客皆笑。

translations.literal: His body resembled it, the sound was true; guests all laughed.
translations.idiomatic: His posture and cry were so lifelike that the mourners burst into laughter.

sentences.zh: 楚顧曰：「諸君不死，而令王濟死乎！」

translations.literal: Chu looked back and said: “You gentlemen do not die, yet you make Wang Ji die!”
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chu glared round and cried, “You lot live on while Wang Ji is dead!”

sentences.zh: 初，濟尚主，主兩目失明，而妒忌尤甚，然終無子，有庶子二人。

translations.literal: In the beginning, when Ji was married to the princess, the princess’s two eyes had lost sight, yet jealousy was especially severe; yet in the end there were no sons; there were two sons by concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, when Wang Ji wed the princess, she was blind in both eyes and fiercely jealous; the couple had no sons of their own but two sons by concubines.

sentences.zh: 卓字文宣，嗣渾爵，拜給事中。

translations.literal: Zhuo, courtesy name Wenxuan, succeeded to Hun’s noble rank, and was appointed Palace Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: The elder, Wang Zhuo, style Wenxuan, inherited Wang Hun’s title and was appointed a Palace Assistant.

sentences.zh: 次聿，字茂宣，襲公主封敏陽侯。

translations.literal: Next Yu, courtesy name Maoxuan, inherited the princess’s enfeoffment as Marquis of Minyang.
translations.idiomatic: The younger, Wang Yu, style Maoxuan, succeeded to the princess’s fief as Marquis of Minyang.

sentences.zh: 濟二弟，澄字道深，汶字茂深，皆辯慧有才藻，並曆清顯。

translations.literal: Ji had two younger brothers: Cheng, courtesy name Daoshen, and Wen, courtesy name Maoshen; both were eloquent and clever with literary talent, and together passed through pure and eminent posts.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji’s brothers Wang Cheng (style Daoshen) and Wang Wen (style Maoshen) were both quick-witted and literary, rising through prestigious clean posts.

sentences.zh: 王濬

translations.literal: Biographical section heading: Wang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun

sentences.zh: 王濬，字士治，弘農湖人也。

translations.literal: Wang Jun, courtesy name Shizhi, was a man of Huren in Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun, courtesy name Shizhi, was a native of Huren in Hongnong commandery.

sentences.zh: 家世二千石。

translations.literal: For generations his family had been two-thousand-*dan* [officials].
translations.idiomatic: His family had for generations held offices at the two-thousand-*dan* level.

sentences.zh: 濬博墳典，美姿貌，不修名行，不為鄉曲所稱。

translations.literal: Jun was broadly learned in the tombs and canons, handsome in bearing and appearance; he did not cultivate reputation and conduct, and was not praised by village and district.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun was widely read in the classics, comely in person, yet indifferent to reputation and local opinion never singled him out.

sentences.zh: 晚乃變節，疏通亮達，恢廓有大志。

translations.literal: Only late did he change his course, becoming open, lucid, and penetrating, magnanimous with great aims.
translations.idiomatic: Only later did he mend his ways, emerging open-minded, far-sighted, and ambitious on a grand scale.

sentences.zh: 嘗起宅，開門前路廣數十步。

translations.literal: He once built a house, opening the road before the gate several tens of paces wide.
translations.idiomatic: When he built a residence, he laid a roadway dozens of paces wide before the gate.

sentences.zh: 人或謂之何太過，濬曰：「吾欲使容長戟幡旗。

translations.literal: Someone said to him why so excessive; Jun said: “I wish to make it hold long halberds and banner flags.”
translations.idiomatic: Asked why so extravagant, he said he meant to leave room for long halberds and ceremonial banners.

sentences.zh: 」眾咸笑之，濬曰：「陳勝有言，燕雀安知鴻鵠之志。

translations.literal: The crowd all laughed at him; Jun said: “Chen Sheng had a saying: how can swallows and sparrows know the aims of the wild swan?”
translations.idiomatic: The crowd mocked him; Wang Jun quoted Chen Sheng: “How should sparrows grasp the wild goose’s design?”

sentences.zh: 」州郡辟河東從事。

translations.literal: The province and commandery summoned him as clerk in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He received provincial and commandery appointment as a clerk in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 守令有不廉潔者，皆望風自引而去。

translations.literal: Magistrates who were not incorrupt all, catching his wind, withdrew of themselves and left.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt county magistrates, catching word of him, resigned and fled.

sentences.zh: 刺史燕國徐邈有女才淑，擇夫未嫁。

translations.literal: Inspector Xu Miao of Yan had a daughter talented and virtuous, and in choosing a husband had not yet married her.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao, Yan-country inspector, had a gifted, virtuous daughter still unmarried while he sought a match.

sentences.zh: 邈乃大會佐吏，令女於內觀之。

translations.literal: Miao thereupon greatly assembled his subordinate clerks, and ordered the daughter to observe them from within.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao then gathered his staff and had his daughter view them from an inner room.

sentences.zh: 女指濬告母，邈遂妻之。

translations.literal: The daughter pointed to Jun and told her mother; Miao thereupon gave her to him as wife.
translations.idiomatic: She singled out Wang Jun and told her mother; Xu Miao married her to him.

sentences.zh: 後參征南軍事，羊祜深知待之。

translations.literal: Afterward he joined the staff of the south-conquering army; Yang Hu deeply knew and treated him well.
translations.idiomatic: He later served on the staff of the southern expedition; Yang Hu valued him highly.

sentences.zh: 祜兄子暨白祜：「濬為人志太，奢侈不節，不可專任，宜有以裁之。

translations.literal: Hu’s elder brother’s son Ji said to Hu: “Jun as a man has aims too great, is extravagant and unbridled; he cannot be solely entrusted; there ought to be something to restrain him.”
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu’s nephew Yang Ji warned him, “Wang Jun’s ambitions run high and his spending knows no limit; do not rely on him alone—he needs checks.”

sentences.zh: 」祜曰：「濬有大才，將欲濟其所欲，必可用也。

translations.literal: Hu said: “Jun has great talent; I am about to help him realize what he desires—he must be usable.”
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu replied, “Wang Jun has great ability; if I help him achieve his aims, he will prove indispensable.”

sentences.zh: 」轉車騎從事中郎，識者謂祜可謂能舉善焉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant Clerk to the General of Chariots and Cavalry; knowledgeable persons said Hu could be called able to promote the good.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun was moved to Attendant Clerk under the General of Chariots and Cavalry; observers praised Yang Hu for knowing how to elevate worthy men.

sentences.zh: 除巴郡太守。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Ba commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Governor of Ba.

sentences.zh: 郡邊吳境，兵士苦役，生男多不養。

translations.literal: The commandery bordered Wu territory; soldiers suffered bitter corvée; when sons were born many were not reared.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery adjoined Wu; conscripts were crushed by labor, and families often refused to rear newborn boys.

sentences.zh: 濬乃嚴其科條，寬其徭課，其產育者皆與休復，所全活者數千人。

translations.literal: Jun thereupon made strict his regulations and articles, and relaxed his labor and tax levies; those who bore children all received rest and remission; those wholly kept alive numbered several thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun tightened statutes but eased labor and taxes, granting rest and exemptions to new parents—thus saving thousands of infants.

sentences.zh: 轉廣漢太守，垂惠布政，百姓賴之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Guanghan, spreading kindness and extending government; the hundred surnames relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Guanghan, he ruled with benevolent policies on which the people depended.

sentences.zh: 濬夜夢懸三刀於臥屋梁上，須臾又益一刀，濬警覺，意甚惡之。

translations.literal: Jun at night dreamed three knives hung on the crossbeam of his sleeping chamber; in a moment there was again an increase of one knife; Jun startled awake, and his thoughts were very ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun dreamed of three knives hanging from his bedroom rafter, then a fourth appeared; he woke in alarm, sensing ill omen.

sentences.zh: 主簿李毅再拜賀曰：「三刀為州字，又益一者，明府其臨益州乎？

translations.literal: Chief clerk Li Yi twice bowed in congratulation and said: “Three knives make the character for ‘province’; again increasing one—my lord, is it that you will face Yizhou?”
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Li Yi bowed twice and said, “Three blades form the character *zhou* ‘province’; a fourth hints you will govern Yizhou.”

sentences.zh: 」及賊張弘殺益州刺史皇甫晏，果遷濬為益州刺史。

translations.literal: When the bandit Zhang Hong killed Inspector of Yizhou Huangfu Yan, indeed Jun was promoted to be Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When rebel Zhang Hong murdered Inspector Huangfu Yan of Yizhou, Wang Jun was duly promoted to that post.

sentences.zh: 濬設方略，悉誅弘等，以勳封關內侯。

translations.literal: Jun set plans and methods, and wholly executed Hong and the rest; by merit he was enfeoffed Marquis Within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun devised strategy, exterminated Zhang Hong’s band, and earned a Marquis Within the Passes enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 懷輯殊俗，待以威信，蠻夷徼外，多來歸降。

translations.literal: He cherished and gathered strange customs, treating them with awe-inspiring trustworthiness; Man and Yi beyond the pale for the most part came to submit and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified frontier peoples with consistent good faith, and many tribes beyond the passes came to surrender.

sentences.zh: 徵拜右衛將軍，除大司農。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed General of the Right Guard, and appointed Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as General of the Right Guard and named Grand Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 車騎將軍羊祜雅知濬有奇略，乃密表留濬，於是重拜益州刺史。

translations.literal: General of Chariots and Cavalry Yang Hu by refined understanding knew Jun had strange stratagems, and thereupon secretly memorialized to retain Jun; at this he was again appointed Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: General of Chariots and Cavalry Yang Hu, discerning Wang Jun’s strategic gifts, secretly memorialized to keep him; Wang Jun was therefore reappointed Inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 武帝謀伐吳，詔濬修舟艦。

translations.literal: The Martial Emperor planned to attack Wu, and ordered Jun to repair boats and ships.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu planned the conquest of Wu, he ordered Wang Jun to build warships.

sentences.zh: 濬乃作大船連舫，方百二十步，受二千餘人。

translations.literal: Jun thereupon made great ships linked as barges, square one hundred twenty paces, holding over two thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun built massive linked barges, each deck one hundred twenty paces square, carrying more than two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 以木為城，起樓櫓，開四出門，其上皆得馳馬來往。

translations.literal: With wood he made walls, raised towered watchtowers, opened four gates going out; on them all one could gallop horses back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: Timber palisades crowned with fighting towers ringed four gates; cavalry could ride at full speed along the decks.

sentences.zh: 又畫鷁首怪獸於船首，以懼江神。

translations.literal: Again he painted *yi*-bird heads and strange beasts on the ship prows, so as to frighten the river gods.
translations.idiomatic: He painted *yi*-bird figureheads and monstrous beasts on the bows to overawe the river spirits.

sentences.zh: 舟楫之盛，自古未有。

translations.literal: The flourishing of boats and oars, from antiquity there had not been.
translations.idiomatic: Never had such a flotilla been seen.

sentences.zh: 濬造船於蜀，其木柿蔽江而下。

translations.literal: Jun built ships in Shu; their wood shavings covered the river going down.
translations.idiomatic: As Wang Jun built his fleet in Shu, scrap wood choked the current downstream.

sentences.zh: 吳建平太守吾彥取流柿以呈孫皓曰：「晉必有攻吳之計，宜增建平兵。

translations.literal: Wu’s Governor of Jianping, Wu Yan, took the flowing shavings and presented them to Sun Hao, saying: “Jin surely has a plan to attack Wu; it is fitting to increase Jianping’s troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yan, Wu’s governor of Jianping, caught the drifting chips and urged Sun Hao, “Jin is preparing to strike Wu—send more troops to Jianping.

sentences.zh: 建平不下，終不敢渡。

translations.literal: If Jianping is not taken, in the end they will not dare cross.
translations.idiomatic: Unless Jianping falls, they will never dare cross the river.”

sentences.zh: 」皓不從。

translations.literal: Hao did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao ignored him.

sentences.zh: 尋以謠言拜濬為龍驤將軍、監梁益諸軍事。

translations.literal: Soon, because of a prophecy-ballad, Jun was appointed General Soaring Dragon and overseer of military affairs in Liang and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a circulating prophecy led to Wang Jun’s appointment as Dragon-Soaring General with command over Liang and Yi forces.

sentences.zh: 語在《羊祜傳》。

translations.literal: The words are in the ‘Biography of Yang Hu.’
translations.idiomatic: The details appear in the biography of Yang Hu.

sentences.zh: 時朝議咸諫伐吳，濬乃上疏曰：「臣數參訪吳楚同異，孫皓荒淫凶逆，荊揚賢愚無不嗟怨。

translations.literal: At the time court deliberation all remonstrated against attacking Wu; Jun thereupon presented a memorial saying: “Your servant has repeatedly investigated the sameness and difference of Wu and Chu; Sun Hao is dissolute, cruel, and rebellious; in Jing and Yang the worthy and foolish alike none do not sigh in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When the court almost unanimously opposed attacking Wu, Wang Jun memorialized that he had repeatedly compared Wu and Chu, that Sun Hao was debauched, cruel, and perverse, and that every class in Jing and Yang groaned with resentment.

sentences.zh: 且觀時運，宜速征伐。

translations.literal: Moreover, observing the times and fate, it is fitting speedily to campaign and attack.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, he argued, the trend of the times demanded a rapid campaign.

sentences.zh: 若今不伐，天變難預。

translations.literal: If now we do not attack, heaven’s changes are hard to foresee.
translations.idiomatic: To delay now was to risk heavenly shifts no one could predict.

sentences.zh: 令皓卒死，更立賢主，文武各得其所，則強敵也。

translations.literal: If Hao suddenly dies, and they replace him with a worthy ruler, civil and military each obtaining their place, then it is a strong enemy.
translations.idiomatic: If Sun Hao died and a worthy successor brought order to civil and military posts, Wu would become a formidable enemy.

sentences.zh: 臣作船七年，日有朽敗，又臣年已七十，死亡無日。

translations.literal: Your servant has made ships seven years; daily there is rot and ruin; moreover your servant’s years are already seventy; death is not distant.
translations.idiomatic: He had spent seven years on the fleet, which rotted day by day; at seventy, death could come any moment.

sentences.zh: 三者一乖，則難圖也，誠願陛下無失事機。

translations.literal: If these three are once at odds, then it is hard to plan; I sincerely wish Your Majesty not to miss the moment for action.
translations.idiomatic: Should any one of those three fall out of step, the whole design fails; I urge you not to let the opportunity slip.

sentences.zh: 」帝深納焉。

translations.literal: ” The emperor deeply accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: ” The emperor took the advice to heart.

sentences.zh: 賈充、荀勖陳諫以為不可，唯張華固勸。

translations.literal: Jia Chong and Xun Xu presented remonstrance holding it could not be done; only Zhang Hua firmly urged [it].
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong and Xun Xu argued against the campaign; Zhang Hua alone pressed strongly for it.

sentences.zh: 又杜預表請，帝乃發詔，分命諸方節度。

translations.literal: Again Du Yu memorialized requesting; the emperor then issued an edict, dividing orders to the various regional commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu again petitioned for action, whereupon the emperor promulgated an edict assigning commanders on each front.

sentences.zh: 濬於是統兵。

translations.literal: Jun thereupon commanded the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun then took command of the army.

sentences.zh: 先在巴郡之所全育者，皆堪徭役供軍，其父母戒之曰：「王府君生爾，爾必勉之，無愛死也！」

translations.literal: Those whom he had earlier at Ba commandery wholly nurtured to life were all fit for corvée labor to supply the army; their parents admonished them, saying: “Prefect Wang gave you life—you must exert yourselves; do not shrink from death!”
translations.idiomatic: The people he had once saved in Ba were now liable for levy and could serve the host; their parents warned them, “Prefect Wang spared your lives—strive your hardest and do not cling to life timidly.”

sentences.zh: 正月，濬發自成都，率巴東監軍、廣武將軍唐彬攻吳丹楊，克之，擒其丹楊監盛紀。

translations.literal: In the first month, Jun set out from Chengdu, leading the Supervising Army of Badong and General Who Extends Military Might Tang Bin to attack Wu’s Danyang, took it, and captured its Danyang Supervisor Sheng Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month Wang Jun marched from Chengdu with Tang Bin, Supervising Army of Badong and General Who Extends Military Might, struck Wu’s Danyang, reduced it, and seized the local supervisor Sheng Ji.

sentences.zh: 吳人于江險磧要害之處，並以鐵鎖橫截之，又作鐵錐長丈餘，暗置江中，以逆距船。

translations.literal: The Wu men at places in the river’s perilous shallows and critical points all moreover used iron chains to block them crosswise; they also made iron spikes over a *zhang* in length, secretly set them in the river, to oppose and repel ships.
translations.idiomatic: Where the Yangtze ran shallow and treacherous, the Wu defenders stretched iron chains across the channel and sank iron spikes, each over ten feet long, to snag incoming hulls.

sentences.zh: 先是，羊祜獲吳間諜，具知情狀。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yang Hu had captured a Wu spy and fully knew the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu had earlier taken a Wu agent and learned every detail of their defenses.

sentences.zh: 濬乃作大筏數十，亦方百餘步，縛草為人，被甲持杖，令善水者以筏先行，筏遇鐵錐，錐輒著筏去。

translations.literal: Jun then made several dozen large rafts, also over a hundred paces square, bound straw into men, armored them and had them hold weapons, ordered skilled swimmers to take the rafts ahead first; when a raft met an iron spike, the spike always stuck to the raft and was carried off.
translations.idiomatic: Jun built scores of huge rafts—each over a hundred paces to a side—rigged with straw dummies in armor; strong swimmers poled them ahead so the submerged spikes snagged the rafts and tore free.

sentences.zh: 又作火炬，長十餘丈，大數十圍，灌以麻油，在船前，遇鎖，然炬燒之，須臾，融液斷絕，於是船無所礙。

translations.literal: He also made torches, over ten *zhang* long, dozens of *wei* in girth, poured sesame oil into them, placed them before the ships; when they met chains, they lit the torches and burned them; in a moment, [the metal] melted and broke apart, and so the ships had no obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: He also fashioned enormous oiled torches, set them on the prows, and when they reached the chains set them alight; the iron melted through in moments and the fleet passed unhindered.

sentences.zh: 二月庚申，克吳西陵，獲其鎮南將軍留憲、征南將軍成據、宜都太守虞忠。

translations.literal: On *gengshen* in the second month, he took Wu’s Xiling and captured their General Who Garrisons the South Liu Xian, General Who Conquers the South Cheng Ju, and Administrator of Yidu Yu Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: On *gengshen* in the second month he seized Xiling, taking Liu Xian, Cheng Ju, and Yidu prefect Yu Zhong.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，克荊門、夷道二城，獲監軍陸晏。

translations.literal: On *renxu*, he took the two cities Jingmen and Yidao and captured Supervising Army Lu Yan.
translations.idiomatic: On *renxu* he reduced Jingmen and Yidao and captured Lu Yan, the army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，克樂鄉，獲水軍督陸景。

translations.literal: On *yichou*, he took Lexiang and captured Naval Commander Lu Jing.
translations.idiomatic: On *yichou* he took Lexiang and made prisoner the naval commander Lu Jing.

sentences.zh: 平西將軍施洪等來降。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the West Shi Hong and others came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hong, General Who Pacifies the West, and others defected to Jin.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，詔進濬為平東將軍、假節、都督益梁諸軍事。

translations.literal: On *yihai*, an edict advanced Jun to General Who Pacifies the East, granted credential axes, and made him Area Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Yi and Liang.
translations.idiomatic: On *yihai* he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East with ceremonial axes and overall command in Yi and Liang.

sentences.zh: 濬自發蜀，兵不血刃，攻無堅城，夏口、武昌，無相支抗。

translations.literal: From the time Jun set out from Shu, the soldiers did not bloody blades; in attack there was no stubborn city; Xiakou and Wuchang had none to mutually support and resist.
translations.idiomatic: From his departure from Shu his advance drew hardly a drop of blood; no city long held out, and Xiakou and Wuchang offered no coordinated defense.

sentences.zh: 於是順流鼓棹，徑造三山。

translations.literal: Thereupon following the current he beat the oars and went straight to make Sanshan.
translations.idiomatic: He then swept downstream with drums and oars and made straight for Sanshan.

sentences.zh: 皓遣遊擊將軍張象率舟軍萬人禦濬，象軍望旗而降。

translations.literal: Hao sent Mobile Strike General Zhang Xiang to lead a naval force of ten thousand to oppose Jun; Xiang’s army, seeing the banners, surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao dispatched Zhang Xiang with ten thousand men to intercept Jun, but Zhang’s fleet lowered its flags and capitulated at sight.

sentences.zh: 皓聞濬軍旌旗器甲，屬天滿江，威勢甚盛，莫不破膽。

translations.literal: When Hao heard that Jun’s army’s banners, weapons, and armor filled heaven and the whole river, its awesomeness was very great, none did not break gall.
translations.idiomatic: Word that Jun’s arms and banners masked sky and river struck Sun Hao’s court with terror.

sentences.zh: 用光祿薛瑩、中書令胡沖計，送降文於濬曰：「吳郡孫皓叩頭死罪。

translations.literal: Employing the plan of Household Affairs Grandee Xue Ying and Palace Secretariat Director Hu Chong, he sent a surrender document to Jun, saying: “Sun Hao of Wu commandery knocks his head—crime deserving death.
translations.idiomatic: On the advice of Xue Ying and Hu Chong he sent Jun a deed of surrender opening, “Sun Hao of Wu kowtows in guilt.

sentences.zh: 昔漢室失禦，九州幅裂，先人因時略有江南，遂阻山河，與魏乖隔。

translations.literal: Formerly the Han house lost the reins; the nine provinces split like a bolt of cloth; my forebears by the times briefly took the south of the Yangtze, thereupon blocked by mountains and rivers, and with Wei fell apart and were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: When Han rule collapsed and the realm shattered, our ancestors seized a foothold south of the Long River and held it apart from Wei.

sentences.zh: 大晉龍興，德覆四海，暗劣偷安，未喻天命。

translations.literal: The great Jin rose like a dragon; its virtue overspread the four seas; [we,] dim and inferior, stole peace, and did not comprehend Heaven’s mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Great Jin arose in majesty and its benevolence covered the world; we clung to a precarious peace and failed to read Heaven’s will.

sentences.zh: 至於今者，猥煩六軍，衡蓋露次，還臨江渚。

translations.literal: As for the present, we have rudely troubled the six armies; umbrellas and canopies bivouac in the open, turning back to face the river’s islets.
translations.idiomatic: Now your hosts have humbled us; imperial regalia stand encamped along the bank as you wheel back toward our shores.

sentences.zh: 舉國震惶，假息漏刻，敢緣天朝，含弘光大。

translations.literal: The whole state trembles in fear, borrows breath by the water-clock’s drip, yet dares, by the celestial court’s vast, bright enlargement, [to hope].
translations.idiomatic: The realm quakes; we cling to each borrowed hour, yet dare appeal to the dynasty’s boundless grace.

sentences.zh: 謹遣私署太常張夔等奉所佩璽綬，委質請命。

translations.literal: Respectfully I dispatch my privately appointed Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Kui and others to present the jade seals and ribbons I wear, submit hostages, and beg for my life.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore send Zhang Kui, whom I had styled Minister of Ceremonies, with the seals and cords of office, to offer submission and sue for mercy.

sentences.zh: 」壬寅，濬入於石頭。

translations.literal: ” On *renyin*, Jun entered Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: ” On *renyin* Wang Jun entered Shitou fortress.

sentences.zh: 皓乃備亡國之禮，素車白馬，肉袒面縛，銜璧牽羊，大夫衰服，士輿櫬，率其偽太子瑾、瑾弟魯王虔等二十一人，造於壘門。

translations.literal: Hao then prepared the rites of a fallen state—plain cart and white horse, bared torso with bound hands, jade disk in mouth leading a sheep, great officers in mourning dress, scholars bearing a bier—leading his false heir apparent Jin, Jin’s younger brother the Prince of Lu Qian, and twenty-one others, and came to the camp gate.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao then performed the full ritual of a defeated sovereign—unadorned carriage, white horses, stripped and bound, jade and sheep in hand, ministers in sackcloth, a coffin borne before him—and with his heir Sima Jin, the Prince of Lu Qian, and twenty-one others presented himself at Jun’s camp.

sentences.zh: 濬躬解其縛，受璧焚櫬，送于京師。

translations.literal: Jun personally undid his bonds, accepted the jade, burned the bier, and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jun himself cut his bonds, took the offering jade, burned the surrender coffin as rite required, and sent him north to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 收其圖籍，封其府庫，軍無私焉。

translations.literal: He collected their maps and registers, sealed their treasuries, and the army took nothing for private gain.
translations.idiomatic: He secured maps and census rolls, sealed the storehouses, and kept the troops from looting.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使者犒濬軍。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched envoys to reward Jun’s army.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent envoys to feast and commend Jun’s command.

sentences.zh: 初，詔書使濬下建平，受杜預節度，至秣陵，受王渾節度。

translations.literal: At first, the edict ordered Jun to go down to Jianping and submit to Du Yu’s direction; on reaching Moling, to submit to Wang Hun’s direction.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the edict told Jun to take Jianping under Du Yu’s orders, then Moling under Wang Hun’s.

sentences.zh: 預至江陵，謂諸將帥曰：「若濬得下建平，則順流長驅，威名已著，不宜令受制於我。

translations.literal: When Yu reached Jiangling, he said to the various generals: “If Jun can take Jianping, then he will drive straight downcurrent; his prestige will already be established—it is not fitting to make him receive constraint from me.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangling Du Yu told his officers that if Wang Jun took Jianping he would sweep downstream with reputation already won and ought not be made subordinate to Du’s command

sentences.zh: 若不能克，則無緣得施節度。

translations.literal: If he cannot overcome [it], then there is no occasion to apply direction.”
translations.idiomatic: , and that if Jun failed, there was no point in Du’s exercising direction over him.

sentences.zh: 」濬至西陵，預與之書曰：'足下既摧其西籓，便當徑取秣陵，討累世之逋寇，釋吳人於塗炭。

translations.literal: ” When Jun reached Xiling, Yu wrote him a letter, saying: ‘You have already crushed their western screen; you ought to go straight to take Moling, punish the fugitive foe of many generations, and release the Wu people from mud and charcoal.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiling Du Yu wrote that Jun had shattered Wu’s western shield and should press straight on to Moling, destroy the foe of many generations, and free the Wu people from ruin.

sentences.zh: 自江入淮，逾於泗汴，溯河而上，振旅還都，亦曠世一事也。

translations.literal: From the Yangtze into the Huai, crossing Si and Bian, ascend the Yellow River upward, shake the host and return to the capital—this too is a deed of an age.”
translations.idiomatic: From the Yangtze into the Huai, across the Si and Bian, up the Yellow River, he could shake out the host and return to the capital—a feat for the ages.

sentences.zh: 」濬大悅，表呈預書。

translations.literal: ” Jun was greatly pleased and memorialized presenting Yu’s letter.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was delighted and forwarded Du Yu’s letter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 及濬將至秣陵，王渾遣信要令暫過論事，濬舉帆直指，報曰：「風利，不得泊也。

translations.literal: When Jun was about to reach Moling, Wang Hun sent a messenger demanding he stop briefly to discuss matters; Jun raised sail and pointed straight [on], replying: “The wind is favorable; I cannot anchor.
translations.idiomatic: As Jun neared Moling, Wang Hun sent word asking him to pause for a conference; Jun filled his sails and replied that the wind favored him and he could not put in.

sentences.zh: 」王渾久破皓中軍，斬張悌等，頓兵不敢進。

translations.literal: ” Wang Hun long since had broken Hao’s central army, beheaded Zhang Ti and others, halted the troops and dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun had already shattered Sun Hao’s main force and beheaded Zhang Ti and others, yet held his troops idle and dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 而濬乘勝納降，渾恥而且忿，乃表濬違詔不受節度，誣罪狀之。

translations.literal: But Jun, riding victory, accepted the surrender; Hun was ashamed and moreover resentful; thereupon he memorialized that Jun had disobeyed the edict and not accepted direction, and slanderously charged him.
translations.idiomatic: Jun, however, carried the day and took the capitulation; Hun, humiliated and furious, accused him of defying orders and slandered him at court.

sentences.zh: 有司遂按濬檻車征，帝弗許，詔讓濬曰：「伐國事重，宜令有一。

translations.literal: The authorities thereupon pressed for Jun to be summoned in a prison cart; the emperor did not permit it, and an edict reproved Jun, saying: “Subduing a state is weighty; it is fitting that there be unity.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry urged Jun’s arrest in a caged cart; the emperor refused and rebuked him, saying that subduing a state was a grave matter and command ought to be unified.

sentences.zh: 前詔使將軍受安車將軍渾節度，渾思謀深重，案甲以待將軍。
