translations.literal: The prior edict ordered the general to submit to the direction of General of the Peaceful Chariot Hun; Hun’s plans and deliberations are deep and weighty; he rested armor to await the general.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier edict had placed him under Wang Hun, General of the Peaceful Chariot, whose plans ran deep; Hun had rested his armor and awaited the general.

sentences.zh: 云何徑前，不從渾命，違制昧利，甚失大義。

translations.literal: How could you go straight forward, not follow Hun’s command, violate regulation and obscure profit—greatly losing great righteousness?
translations.idiomatic: How could Jun press straight on, defy Hun’s orders, break regulations for advantage, and abandon paramount duty?

sentences.zh: 將軍功勳，簡在朕心，當率由詔書，崇成王法，而於事終恃功肆意，朕將何以令天下？

translations.literal: The general’s merit and achievement are recorded in my heart; you ought to follow the edicts and exaltingly complete the king’s law—yet in the end you relied on merit and acted as you pleased; with what shall I order the realm?”
translations.idiomatic: Your merit is written on my heart; you should follow edict and exalt the king’s law—yet in the end you leaned on your achievement and indulged your will. With what am I to command All under Heaven?”

sentences.zh: 」濬上書自理曰：

translations.literal: ” Jun memorialized in his own defense, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Jun submitted a lengthy memorial in his own defense.

sentences.zh: 渾又騰周浚書，雲濬軍得吳寶物。

translations.literal: Hun again forwarded Zhou Jun’s letter, saying Jun’s army had obtained Wu treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Hun also circulated Zhou Jun’s letter claiming Jun’s men had plundered Wu’s riches.

sentences.zh: 濬復表曰：

translations.literal: Jun again memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Jun answered with another memorial:

sentences.zh: 濬至京都，有司奏，濬表既不列前後所被七詔月日，又赦後違詔不受渾節度，大不敬，付廷尉科罪。

translations.literal: When Jun reached the capital, the authorities reported that Jun’s memorial neither listed the dates of the seven edicts he had received before and after, nor, after the amnesty, [noted his] disobeying the edict and not accepting Hun’s direction—great irreverence—and he should be handed to the Commandant of Justice for sentencing.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital the ministry charged that his memorial omitted the dates of seven imperial orders and that, even after amnesty, he had defied Wang Hun—capital offense—and should be remanded to the Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「濬前受詔徑造秣陵，後乃下受渾節度。

translations.literal: An edict said: “Jun earlier received an edict to go straight to Moling; afterward there came the order to submit to Hun’s direction.
translations.idiomatic: The edict said that Jun had first received orders to go straight to Moling and only afterward been told to submit to Wang Hun’s direction.

sentences.zh: 詔書稽留，所下不至，便令與不受詔同責，未為經通。

translations.literal: The edicts were delayed in transmission; what was issued did not arrive—to then make him share the blame of one who did not receive an edict is not a constant, comprehensive way.”
translations.idiomatic: Because the orders were held up and never reached him in time, to treat him like a man who had never received an edict was neither fair nor sound.

sentences.zh: 濬不即表上被渾宣詔，此可責也。

translations.literal: That Jun did not immediately memorialize having received the edict as proclaimed by Hun—this may be reproved.
translations.idiomatic: Jun might be reproved for not promptly reporting the edict Hun had announced.

sentences.zh: 濬有征伐之勞，不足以一眚掩之。

translations.literal: Jun has the toil of campaigning; it is not enough for one fault to cover it.
translations.idiomatic: He had borne the hardships of campaigning; one lapse should not efface that.

sentences.zh: 」有司又奏，濬赦後燒賊船百三十五艘，輒敕付廷尉禁推。

translations.literal: ” The authorities again reported that after the amnesty Jun had burned 135 enemy ships, and [the emperor] abruptly ordered him handed to the Commandant of Justice and forbidden investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Officials again charged that after the amnesty Jun had burned 135 enemy ships and pressed to remand him to the Commandant of Justice for a barred inquiry.

sentences.zh: 詔曰「勿推」。

translations.literal: An edict said, “Do not investigate.”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said simply, “No inquiry.”

sentences.zh: 拜濬輔國大將軍，領步兵校尉。

translations.literal: [The court] appointed Jun General Who Aids the State, concurrent Colonel of Foot Soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He was named General Who Aids the State and Colonel of the Foot-Soldier garrison.

sentences.zh: 舊校唯五，置此營自濬始也。

translations.literal: Of old the colonelcies were only five; establishing this camp began with Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Previously there had been only five colonelcies; this sixth camp was created for Jun.

sentences.zh: 有司又奏，輔國依比，未為達官，不置司馬，不給官騎。

translations.literal: The authorities again reported that, by precedent comparison, General Who Aids the State was not yet a lofty office; it did not place an adjutant and did not grant official mounted escorts.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry noted that, by rank tables, General Who Aids the State still lacked a chief of staff and formal mounted guard.

sentences.zh: 詔依征鎮給五百大車，增兵五百人為輔國營，給親騎百人、官騎十人，置司馬。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that, following the model for generals who conquer and garrison, he be given five hundred large carts, five hundred additional soldiers for the Aiding-the-State camp, one hundred personal riders and ten official riders, and an adjutant be placed.
translations.idiomatic: The throne granted him field allowances matching a frontier commander: five hundred supply wagons, five hundred extra troops, a hundred household riders, ten escort horsemen, and a staff adjutant.

sentences.zh: 封為襄陽縣侯，邑萬戶。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed Marquis of Xiangyang County, with a fief of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He received the marquisate of Xiangyang with revenue from ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 封子彝楊鄉亭侯，邑千五百戶，賜絹萬匹，又賜衣一襲、錢三十萬及食物。

translations.literal: His son Yi was enfeoffed Marquis of Yang Township, with a fief of 1,500 households; he was given ten thousand bolts of silk, and again given one suit of clothes, 300,000 cash, and foodstuffs.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi became marquis of Yang township with fifteen hundred households; the court added ten thousand bolts of silk, a full set of robes, three hundred thousand cash, and provisions.

sentences.zh: 濬自以功大，而為渾父子及豪強所抑，屢為有司所奏，每進見，陳其攻伐之勞，及見枉之狀，或不勝忿憤，徑出不辭。

translations.literal: Jun deemed his merit great, yet was suppressed by Hun father and son and the powerful; repeatedly he was reported on by the authorities; each time he entered audience he set forth the toil of his campaigning and the aspect of his being wronged, or could not overcome indignant rage and went straight out without taking leave.
translations.idiomatic: Convinced his deeds outweighed his rewards, yet blocked by the Hun clan and local magnates and hauled before the ministry again and again, he would recount his campaigns and grievances at audience—or storm out speechless with rage.

sentences.zh: 帝每容恕之。

translations.literal: The emperor each time indulgently forgave him.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign each time overlooked it.

sentences.zh: 益州護軍範通，濬之外親也。

translations.literal: Fan Tong, Protector of the Army in Yi, was Jun’s relative by marriage on the outer side.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Tong, army protector in Yi, was a kinsman by marriage.

sentences.zh: 謂濬曰：「卿功則美矣，然恨所以居美者，未盡善也。

translations.literal: He said to Jun: “Your merit is indeed fine, yet I regret that the way you hold the fine is not yet entirely good.
translations.idiomatic: He told Jun that his achievement was splendid but the way he wore that glory was not yet beyond reproach.

sentences.zh: 」濬曰：「何謂也？

translations.literal: ” Jun said: “What is meant?”
translations.idiomatic: Jun asked what he meant.

sentences.zh: 」通曰：「卿旋旆之日，角巾私第，口不言平吳之事。

translations.literal: ” Tong said: “On the day you turn your banners homeward, wear a scholar’s kerchief in your private residence, and by mouth do not speak of the matter of pacifying Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Tong said that on the day Jun turned his banners homeward he should don a scholar’s kerchief in his private residence and never speak of the conquest of Wu.

sentences.zh: 若有問者，輒曰：'聖主之德，群帥之力，老夫何力之有焉！

translations.literal: If there are those who ask, then always say: ‘It is the sage lord’s virtue, the host of commanders’ strength—what force had this old man!’
translations.idiomatic: If anyone asked, he should always answer that it was the sage ruler’s virtue and his commanders’ strength—what had a greybeard like him done?

sentences.zh: '如斯，顏老之不伐，龔遂之雅對，將何以過之。

translations.literal: ' Like this, Yan’s old man’s not boasting, Gong Sui’s elegant reply—how would they surpass it?
translations.idiomatic: That would match Yan Hui’s refusal to boast or Gong Sui’s tactful replies—who could improve on it?

sentences.zh: 藺生所以屈廉頗，王渾能無愧乎！

translations.literal: This is how Lin Sheng bent Lian Po—could Wang Hun then be without shame!”
translations.idiomatic: It was thus that Lin Xiangru humbled Lian Po—could Wang Hun then be free of shame?”

sentences.zh: 」濬曰：「吾始懼鄧艾之事，畏禍及，不得無言，亦不能遣諸胸中，是吾偏也。

translations.literal: ” Jun said: “I began fearing the affair of Deng Ai; fearing disaster reaching me, I could not but speak; nor could I dispel it from my breast—this is my partiality.
translations.idiomatic: Jun said he had first feared the fate of Deng Ai, dreaded calamity reaching him, and could not but speak; neither could he drive the feeling from his breast—that was his bias.”

sentences.zh: 」時人咸以濬功重報輕，博士秦秀、太子洗馬孟康、前溫令李密等並表訟濬之屈。

translations.literal: ” People of the time all held that Jun’s merit was heavy and his reward light; Erudite Qin Xiu, Household Assistant to the Heir Apparent Meng Kang, former Magistrate of Wen Li Mi, and others together memorialized to litigate Jun’s wrong.
translations.idiomatic: People of the day still thought Jun’s merit heavy and his reward slight; Erudite Qin Xiu, Household Assistant to the Heir Apparent Meng Kang, former magistrate of Wen Li Mi, and others jointly memorialized to redress his wrongs.

sentences.zh: 帝乃遷濬鎮軍大將軍，加散騎常侍，領後軍將軍。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon transferred Jun to General Who Garrisons the Army, added him as Cavalier Attendant at Leisure, and made him concurrent General of the Rear Army as before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then promoted him to General Who Garrisons the Army, added cavalier attendant at leisure, and left him General of the Rear Army as well.

sentences.zh: 王渾詣濬，濬嚴設備衛，然後見之，其相猜防如此。

translations.literal: Wang Hun visited Jun; Jun strictly set up guards and equipment, then saw him—their mutual suspicion and guard were thus.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Hun called, Jun surrounded himself with arms before receiving him—such was their mutual distrust.

sentences.zh: 濬平吳之後，以勳高位重，不復素業自居，乃玉食錦服，縱奢侈以自逸。

translations.literal: After Jun pacified Wu, on account of merit high and position weighty, he no longer kept to plain occupation in his person; thereupon jade food and brocade garments, he gave rein to extravagance to ease himself.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu fell, Jun—now powerful and proud—abandoned frugal habits for fine fare, silk robes, and open luxury.

sentences.zh: 其有辟引，多是蜀人，示不遺故舊也。

translations.literal: In those he summoned and recommended, many were Shu men, to show he did not abandon old associates.
translations.idiomatic: His appointments favored Shu men to prove he had not forgotten old ties.

sentences.zh: 後又轉濬撫軍大將軍、開府儀同三司，加特進，散騎常侍、後軍將軍如故。

translations.literal: Afterward he was again transferred to General Who Sooths the Army, with privilege equal to the Three Offices, added Exalted Marcher, Cavalier Attendant at Leisure and General of the Rear Army as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was later moved to General Who Sooths the Army with independent command matching the Three Dukes, honored as Exalted Marcher, and kept his previous attendant and rear-army posts.

sentences.zh: 卒，時年八十，諡曰武。

translations.literal: He died, aged eighty; his posthumous title was Martial.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty with the posthumous name “Martial.”

sentences.zh: 葬柏谷山，大營塋域，葬垣周四十五里，面別開一門，松柏茂盛。

translations.literal: He was buried on Baigu Mountain; he greatly laid out tomb precincts; the burial enclosure ran forty-five *li* on a side; on the face he separately opened one gate; pines and cypresses were luxuriant.
translations.idiomatic: His tomb on Baigu Mountain sprawled over a forty-five-*li* park with its own gate and thick pine and cypress groves.

sentences.zh: 子矩嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ju inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ju succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 矩弟暢，散騎郎。

translations.literal: Ju’s younger brother Chang was a Gentleman Cavalier Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Ju’s brother Chang served as Gentleman Cavalier Attendant.

sentences.zh: 暢子粹，，武帝詔粹尚潁川公主，仕至魏郡太守。

translations.literal: Chang’s son Cui [, punctuation artifact in source,] the Martial Emperor issued an edict that Cui should marry the Princess of Yingchuan, and rose in office to Grand Administrator of Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chang’s son Cui was ordered by Emperor Wu to marry the Princess of Yingchuan and rose to prefect of Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 濬有二孫，過江不見齒錄。

translations.literal: Jun had two grandsons; after crossing the river they were not seen recorded in the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Jun left two grandsons who, once south of the Yangtze, were struck from the noble registers.

sentences.zh: 安西將軍恆溫鎮江陵，表言之曰：「臣聞崇德賞功，為政之所先；

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the West Huan Wen garrisoned Jiangling and memorialized, saying: “Your subject has heard that exalting virtue and rewarding merit are what government puts first;
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen, General Who Pacifies the West, garrisoned Jiangling and submitted a memorial saying that to honor virtue and reward merit was the first concern of government,

sentences.zh: 興滅繼絕，百王之所務。

translations.literal: raising the extinguished and continuing the severed is what the hundred kings make their business.
translations.idiomatic: and that to restore ruined lines and continue severed sacrifices was the business of every sage king.

sentences.zh: 故德參時雍，則奕世承祀；

translations.literal: Therefore when virtue matches the harmonious age, then generation after generation inherits sacrifice;
translations.idiomatic: When virtue matched an age of harmony, offerings passed down generation after generation;

sentences.zh: 功烈一代，則永錫祚胤。

translations.literal: when merit blazes for one generation, then blessings are forever granted to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: when merit blazed for one reign, blessings extended forever to posterity.

sentences.zh: 案故撫軍王濬曆職內外，任兼文武，料敵制勝，明勇獨斷，義存社稷之利，不顧專輒之罪。

translations.literal: I examine: the former General Who Sooths the Army Wang Jun served in office within and without, his charge joining civil and military; he gauged the enemy and controlled victory, was bright and brave and decided alone; righteousness lay in benefit to the altars of soil and grain, and he did not consider the crime of acting on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: The late General Who Sooths the Army Wang Jun had served at court and in the field, joining civil and martial charge; he sized up the enemy, seized victory, and acted with clear courage and independent resolve, seeking the altars’ good and not counting the offense of acting on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 荷戈長鶩，席捲萬里，僭號之吳，面縛象魏，今皇澤被于九州，玄風洽于區外，襄陽之封，廢而莫續；

translations.literal: Bearing halberds and long lances, rolling up ten thousand *li*, the Wu that usurped the title, bound at the imperial gate—now imperial grace spreads over the nine provinces, mysterious wind harmonizes outside the regions; the enfeoffment of Xiangyang is abolished and not continued;
translations.idiomatic: Arms in hand he rolled up ten thousand *li*, and the Wu that had usurped the title came bound to the imperial gate. Now royal grace bathes the nine provinces and the transforming wind reaches beyond the borders, yet the Xiangyang enfeoffment stands abolished without renewal;

sentences.zh: 恩寵之號，墜於近嗣。

translations.literal: the title of favor and honor has fallen on the near posterity.
translations.idiomatic: marks of favor and honor have slipped from the nearest heirs.

sentences.zh: 遐邇酸懷，臣竊悼之。

translations.literal: Far and near are sour in the breast; your subject privately mourns it.
translations.idiomatic: Near and far harbor bitter grief; your subject mourns it in private.

sentences.zh: 濬今有二孫，年出六十，室如懸磬，糊口江濱，四節蒸嘗，菜羹不給。

translations.literal: Jun now has two grandsons, their years past sixty; their chamber is like a hanging chime-stone; they scrape a living by the river’s edge; at the four seasons’ steamed and autumn offerings, vegetable broth is not supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Jun’s two grandsons are past sixty, their homes bare as a hung chime-stone; they scrape a living along the river and cannot supply even vegetable gruel for the seasonal offerings.

sentences.zh: 昔漢高定業，求樂毅之嗣；

translations.literal: Formerly Han Gao established the enterprise and sought the posterity of Yue Yi;
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu, founding the enterprise, sought out the descendants of Yue Yi;

sentences.zh: 世祖旌賢，建葛亮之胤。

translations.literal: the Martial Progenitor raised the worthy and established Zhuge Liang’s descendant.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu raised the worthy and ennobled Zhuge Liang’s line.

sentences.zh: 夫效忠異代，立功異國，尚通天下之善，使不泯棄，況濬建元勳于當年，著喜慶於身後，靈基托根于南垂，皇祚中興于江左，舊物克彰，神器重耀，豈不由伊人之功力也哉！

translations.literal: Now as for serving loyalty in another age and establishing merit in another state, one still connects to the good of all under Heaven and causes them not to be extinguished and cast aside—how much the more Jun, who established the first merit in that year and showed auspicious celebration on his person after death; his spirit foundation entrusts its root on the southern edge, the imperial house’s fortune mid-restores on the left of the Yangtze; old things are able to be manifest, the divine vessel again shines—is it not from that man’s labor and strength!
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty shown under another sovereign and merit won in another realm still links to the good of all under Heaven and keeps their memory from extinction—how much more Jun, who wrought the founding merit of that age and left blessing on his person after death? His spiritual roots rest on the southern march; the house’s mandate renews east of the Yangtze; old glories reappear and the sacred regalia shines again—was that not this man’s labor and strength?

sentences.zh: 誠宜加恩，少垂矜憫，追錄舊勳，纂錫茅土。

translations.literal: It is truly fitting to add favor, slightly incline pity, pursue recording the old merit, and renew granting fief and earth.
translations.idiomatic: It is truly right to show added grace, extend a measure of pity, record his old merit, and renew a grant of fief and land.

sentences.zh: 則聖朝之恩，宣暢于上，忠臣之志，不墜於地矣。

translations.literal: Then the sage court’s grace will be declared and spread above, and loyal ministers’ intent will not fall to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Then the sage court’s kindness would shine abroad above, and the will of loyal ministers would not fall forgotten to the earth.

sentences.zh: 」卒不見省。

translations.literal: ” In the end it was not examined and approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the memorial was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 唐彬

translations.literal: Tang Bin
translations.idiomatic: Tang Bin

sentences.zh: 唐彬，字儒宗，魯國鄒人也。

translations.literal: Tang Bin, courtesy name Ruzong, was a man of Zou in the state of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Bin, *zi* Ruzong, came from Zou in Lu.

sentences.zh: 父台，太山太守。

translations.literal: His father Tai was Grand Administrator of Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Tang Tai, served as grand administrator of Taishan.

sentences.zh: 彬有經國大度，而不拘行檢。

translations.literal: Bin had ordering-the-realm great capacity, yet was not constrained by conduct and self-restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Bin had the breadth of mind to govern the realm but cared little for conventional propriety.

sentences.zh: 少便弓馬，好遊獵，身長八尺，走及奔鹿，強力兼人。

translations.literal: In youth he was skilled at bow and horse, loved roaming and hunting; his body was eight *chi* tall, in running he caught up with fleeing deer; his strength doubled other men.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he excelled at riding and archery and loved the chase; he stood eight feet tall, could outrun a bolting stag, and possessed strength beyond ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 晚乃敦悅經史，尤明《易經》，隨師受業，還家教授，恆數百人。

translations.literal: Only in later years did he earnestly delight in the classics and histories; he was especially clear on the *Book of Changes*; he followed a teacher to receive instruction, returned home and taught; constantly there were several hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: Later he turned seriously to the classics and histories, with particular mastery of the *Zhou yi*; he studied under a tutor, then taught at home to an audience routinely numbering in the hundreds.

sentences.zh: 初為郡門下掾，轉主簿。

translations.literal: At first he served as a clerk under the commandery’s gate, then was transferred to registrar.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a junior clerk in the commandery administration and was promoted to chief registrar.

sentences.zh: 刺史王沈集諸參佐，盛論距吳之策，以問九郡吏。

translations.literal: The inspector Wang Shen assembled the various aides and staff, grandly discoursing on strategies to resist Wu, and put the question to the clerks of the nine commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Wang Shen convened his staff for a wide-ranging discussion of how to oppose Wu and polled the recorders of the nine commanderies.

sentences.zh: 彬與譙郡主張惲俱陳吳有可兼之勢，沈善其對。

translations.literal: Bin together with Qiao commandery’s registrar Zhang Yun both set forth that Wu had a situation that could be annexed; Shen approved their replies.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Bin and Zhang Yun, registrar of Qiao, both argued that Wu could be overrun; Wang Shen commended their answers.

sentences.zh: 又使彬難言吳未可伐者，而辭理皆屈。

translations.literal: Again he had Bin challenge the words of those who said Wu could not yet be attacked, and in every case their wording and reasoning were bent [defeated].
translations.idiomatic: He then had Tang Bin refute those who claimed Wu was not ripe for attack, and each opponent’s argument collapsed.

sentences.zh: 還遷功曹，舉孝廉，州辟主簿，累遷別駕。

translations.literal: He was returned [to office] and promoted merit evaluator; he was recommended filial and incorrupt; the province summoned him as registrar; by stages he rose to aide-de-camp.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved up to merit evaluator, nominated filial and incorrupt, appointed provincial registrar, and eventually promoted to governor’s chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 彬忠肅公亮，盡規匡救，不顯諫以自彰，又奉使詣相府計事，于時僚佐皆當世英彥，見彬莫不欽悅，稱之于文帝，薦為掾屬。

translations.literal: Bin was loyal, solemn, fair, and bright; he exhausted remonstrance and rescue; he did not display remonstrance to make himself conspicuous; moreover he was sent on mission to the minister’s office to plan affairs—at that time the aides and staff were all the age’s outstanding talents; seeing Bin, none failed to admire and delight, and they praised him to Emperor Wen and recommended him as a bureau subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Bin was loyal, grave, and upright; he remonstrated tirelessly to set things right without parading his counsel for fame. Sent to the chancellor’s headquarters on business, he impressed every eminent man on staff, who spoke of him to Emperor Wen and secured him a post among the clerks.

sentences.zh: 帝以問其參軍孔顥，顥忌其能，良久不答。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon asked his army adviser Kong Hao; Hao envied his ability and for a long time did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to his adviser Kong Hao, who resented Tang Bin’s talent and remained silent.

sentences.zh: 陳騫在坐，斂板而稱曰：「彬之為人，勝騫甚遠。

translations.literal: Chen Qian was seated; he gathered his tablet and declared, saying: “As to Bin’s person, he surpasses Qian by very far.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qian, who was present, straightened his tablet and said, “Tang Bin is far my superior as a man.

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「但能如卿，固未易得，何論於勝。

translations.literal: ” The emperor laughed and said: “But if able to be like you, that is indeed not easily obtained—what talk of surpassing.
translations.idiomatic: ” The emperor smiled and replied, “Merely to match you would be rare enough; we need not speak of surpassing.

sentences.zh: 」因辟彬為鎧曹屬。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he summoned Bin as subordinate of the armory bureau.
translations.idiomatic: ” He thereupon appointed Tang Bin to the armory bureau.

sentences.zh: 帝問曰：「卿何以致辟？

translations.literal: The emperor asked, saying: “By what did you achieve summons?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, “What earned you this appointment?”

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「修業陋巷，觀古人之遺跡，言滿天下無口過，行滿天下無怨惡。

translations.literal: ” He replied, saying: “Cultivating enterprise in a mean lane, viewing the traces left by the ancients—speech fills all under Heaven without mouth fault; conduct fills all under Heaven without resentment and hatred.
translations.idiomatic: ” He answered, “Studying in obscurity and pondering the example of the ancients: one may speak before the world without indiscretion and act before the world without earning ill will.

sentences.zh: 」帝顧四坐曰：「名不虛行。

translations.literal: ” The emperor looked toward the four seats and said: “The name does not travel empty.
translations.idiomatic: ” The emperor glanced at those seated and said, “His reputation is no empty boast.

sentences.zh: 」他日，謂孔顥曰：「近見唐彬，卿受蔽賢之責矣。」

translations.literal: ” Another day, he said to Kong Hao: “Recently I have seen Tang Bin—you have incurred the blame of concealing the worthy.”
translations.idiomatic: ” On another occasion he told Kong Hao, “I have lately met Tang Bin; you stand charged with hiding talent from the throne.”

sentences.zh: 初，鄧艾之誅也，文帝以艾久在隴右，素得士心，一旦夷滅，恐邊情搔動，使彬密察之。

translations.literal: At first, at Deng Ai’s execution, Emperor Wen because Ai had long been on Long’s right and ordinarily won the hearts of the gentry, once he was exterminated, feared border sentiment would be stirred and agitated; he sent Bin secretly to inspect it.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng Ai was put to death, Emperor Wen feared that the Longxi frontier, where Deng had long served and enjoyed the troops’ devotion, might grow restless if he were suddenly destroyed, and secretly dispatched Tang Bin to assess the mood.

sentences.zh: 彬還，白帝曰：「鄧艾忌克詭狹，矜能負才，順從者謂為見事，直言者謂之觸迕。

translations.literal: Bin returned and reported to the emperor, saying: “Deng Ai was jealous and harsh, deceitful and narrow; he boasted ability and trusted talent—those who complied he called understanding of affairs; those who spoke straight he called offending contradiction.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Bin reported, “Deng Ai was suspicious, harsh, and narrow; he prized his own abilities—flatterers he deemed astute, frank men he treated as insubordinate.

sentences.zh: 雖長史司馬，參佐牙門，答對失指，輒見罵辱。

translations.literal: Although chief clerk, major, aides, and headquarters staff—if answers missed the point, he always saw cursing and humiliation.
translations.idiomatic: Even chief clerk, major, and camp staff faced abuse if their replies displeased him.

sentences.zh: 處身無禮，大失人心。

translations.literal: In placing his person he lacked ritual; he greatly lost men’s hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He treated others without courtesy and forfeited the army’s goodwill.

sentences.zh: 又好施行事役，數勞眾力。

translations.literal: Moreover he liked to impose labor service and repeatedly toiled the mass of laborers.
translations.idiomatic: He also habitually imposed corvée and overworked the people.

sentences.zh: 隴右甚患苦之，喜聞其禍，不肯為用。

translations.literal: Long’s right greatly suffered bitterness from him; they delighted to hear of his disaster and were unwilling to be used by him.
translations.idiomatic: Longxi had groaned under his rule; they welcomed his fall and would not rally to him again.

sentences.zh: 今諸軍已至，足以鎮壓內外，願無以為慮。」

translations.literal: Now the various armies have already arrived—sufficient to suppress inside and outside; I wish you not to take it as a worry.”
translations.idiomatic: The imperial forces now on the scene are ample to hold the region; Your Majesty need not worry.”

sentences.zh: 俄除尚書水部郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed gentleman of the Masters of Writing for water works.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was named director of the Water Section in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi, he was granted noble rank *guanneihou*.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Taishi era he received the title of secondary marquis.

sentences.zh: 出補鄴令，彬道德齊禮，期月化成。

translations.literal: He went out to fill Ye county magistrate; Bin with virtue aligned ritual; in one full cycle he transformed and completed.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as magistrate of Ye, he led by moral example and ritual, and within a year the district was transformed.

sentences.zh: 遷弋陽太守，明設禁防，百姓安之。

translations.literal: He was promoted Yiyang grand administrator; he clearly established prohibitions and defenses; the hundred surnames were secure in it.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to grand administrator of Yiyang, he enforced clear laws and defenses, and the people lived at ease.

sentences.zh: 以母喪去官。

translations.literal: Because of his mother’s mourning he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 益州東接吳寇，監軍位缺，朝議用武陵太守楊宗及彬。

translations.literal: Yizhou on the east adjoined Wu raiders; the post of supervising army was vacant; court deliberation employed Wuling grand administrator Yang Zong and Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou bordered Wu on the east; with the army supervisor’s post empty, the court debated appointing either Yang Zong, grand administrator of Wuling, or Tang Bin.

sentences.zh: 武帝以問散騎常侍文立，立曰：「宗、彬俱不可失。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu thereupon asked Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary Wen Li; Li said: “Zong and Bin both cannot be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu consulted Wen Li, Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary, who replied, “You cannot afford to lose either Yang Zong or Tang Bin.

sentences.zh: 然彬多財欲，而宗好酒，惟陛下裁之。

translations.literal: Yet Bin has much wealth-desire, while Zong is fond of wine—only Your Majesty decides it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Tang Bin is acquisitive, while Yang Zong drinks heavily—the choice is yours.”

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「財欲可足，酒者難改。

translations.literal: ” The emperor said: “Wealth-desire can be satisfied; as for wine, it is hard to change.
translations.idiomatic: ” The emperor said, “Greed can be curbed; a drunkard is harder to reform.”

sentences.zh: 」遂用彬。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he employed Bin.
translations.idiomatic: ” He chose Tang Bin.

sentences.zh: 尋又詔彬監巴東諸軍事，加廣武將軍。

translations.literal: Before long again an edict ordered Bin to supervise military affairs of Badong and all, and added General Who Extends Martial Might.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict named him supervisor of military affairs in Badong with the additional title General Who Extends Martial Might.

sentences.zh: 上征吳之策，甚合帝意。

translations.literal: He presented a plan to attack Wu; it greatly matched the emperor’s intent.
translations.idiomatic: His strategy for the Wu campaign matched the emperor’s wishes.

sentences.zh: 後與王濬共伐吳，彬屯據沖要，為眾軍前驅。

translations.literal: Later he together with Wang Jun jointly attacked Wu; Bin encamped and held the choke point, acting as vanguard of the mass of armies.
translations.idiomatic: Later he campaigned against Wu alongside Wang Jun, holding the key approaches and leading the van.

sentences.zh: 每設疑兵，應機制勝，陷西陵、樂鄉，多所擒獲。

translations.literal: Whenever he deployed decoy troops, responding to the moment he controlled victory; he took Xiling and Lexiang, in many cases capturing and seizing.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly used feints, seized opportunities, and took Xiling and Lexiang with heavy captures.

sentences.zh: 自巴陵、沔口以東，諸賊所聚，莫不震懼，倒戈肉袒。

translations.literal: From Baling and Mian’s mouth eastward, wherever the bandits gathered, none failed to tremble in fear; they inverted halberds and bared flesh [torso].
translations.idiomatic: East of Baling and the Han estuary every Wu stronghold quailed; defenders threw down their arms and came out bare-chested to surrender.

sentences.zh: 彬知賊寇已殄，孫皓將降，未至建鄴二百里，稱疾遲留，以示不競。

translations.literal: Bin knew the bandit raiders were already exterminated; Sun Hao was about to surrender; not yet two hundred *li* to Jianye, he claimed illness and delayed, to show not competing.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Wu’s forces broken and Sun Hao ready to yield, he halted two hundred *li* short of Jianye, pleading illness, to avoid the scramble for glory.

sentences.zh: 果有先到者爭物，後到者爭功，于時有識莫不高彬此舉。

translations.literal: Indeed there were those who arrived first who quarreled over goods; those who arrived later who quarreled over merit—at that time those with understanding none failed to esteem Bin for this act.
translations.idiomatic: As it happened, the first arrivals squabbled over booty and the latecomers over credit; informed observers all praised Tang Bin’s restraint.

sentences.zh: 吳平，詔曰：「廣武將軍唐彬受任方隅，東禦吳寇，南監蠻越，撫寧疆埸，有綏禦之績。

translations.literal: With Wu pacified, an edict said: “General Who Extends Martial Might Tang Bin received appointment on a frontier corner; east he resisted Wu raiders; south he supervised Man and Yue; he soothed and quieted the border fields; he had pacifying-and-controlling traces.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu fell, an edict declared, “General Who Extends Martial Might Tang Bin held a border command: he faced Wu in the east, watched the southern tribes, and kept the marches tranquil—true pacification and control.

sentences.zh: 又每慷慨，志在立功。

translations.literal: Moreover at every turn he was stirring and forthright; his intent lay in establishing merit.
translations.idiomatic: He was ardent by nature and bent on achievement.

sentences.zh: 頃者征討，扶疾奉命，首啟戎行，獻俘授馘，勳效顯著。

translations.literal: Recently in the expedition and suppression, supporting illness he received orders; he first opened the martial line; he presented captives and handed over severed-ear tallies; merit and effect were manifest and clear.
translations.idiomatic: In the recent campaign he took the field despite illness, opened the advance, delivered prisoners and trophies, and his service stood out.

sentences.zh: 其以彬為右將軍、都督巴東諸軍事。

translations.literal: Let Bin be made General of the Right, area commander-in-chief of military affairs of Badong and all.
translations.idiomatic: He is appointed General of the Right and area commander for all Badong forces.

sentences.zh: 」徵拜翊軍校尉，改封上庸縣侯，食邑六千戶，賜絹六千匹。

translations.literal: ” He was summoned and appointed Colonel of the Wings of the Army, his enfeoffment changed to marquis of Shangyong county, food households six thousand, silk six thousand bolts granted.
translations.idiomatic: ” He was recalled as Colonel of the Wings of the Army, enfeoffed as marquis of Shangyong with six thousand households and a gift of six thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 朝有疑議，每參預焉。

translations.literal: When the court had doubtful deliberations, he always participated in them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever court debate stalled on a point, he was called in.

sentences.zh: 北虜侵掠北平，以彬為使持節、監幽州諸軍事、領護烏丸校尉、右將軍。

translations.literal: The northern barbarians invaded and plundered Beiping; Bin was made credential bearer, supervisor of military affairs of Youzhou and all, concurrent colonel protecting the Wuhuan, general of the right.
translations.idiomatic: Northern tribes raided Beiping; Tang Bin received the credentials, took charge of Youzhou forces, held the concurrent post of Colonel Protector of the Wuhuan, and kept his rank as General of the Right.

sentences.zh: 彬既至鎮，訓卒利兵，廣農重稼，震威耀武，宣喻國命，示以恩信。

translations.literal: Once Bin arrived at the command, he drilled troops and sharpened weapons, broadly farmed and weighted grain crops, shook might and displayed martial power, proclaimed and made understood the state’s commands, showed them grace and trust.
translations.idiomatic: At his post he trained soldiers, honed weapons, promoted farming, staged demonstrations of force, published imperial policy, and combined awe with good faith.

sentences.zh: 於是鮮卑二部大莫廆、擿何等並遣侍子入貢。

translations.literal: Thereupon the two Xianbei divisions Damowei and Tihe and others together sent hostage sons to enter tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Two Xianbei confederations led by Damowei and Tihe then sent hostages and tribute.

sentences.zh: 兼修學校，誨誘無倦，仁惠廣被。

translations.literal: Concurrently he repaired schools; instructing and leading, he was without weariness; benevolent favor broadly spread.
translations.idiomatic: He restored schools, taught tirelessly, and his kindness reached widely.

sentences.zh: 遂開拓舊境，卻地千里。

translations.literal: Thereupon he opened and expanded the old border; he pushed back territory a thousand *li*.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered old ground and pushed the frontier back a thousand *li*.

sentences.zh: 復秦長城塞，自溫城洎于碣石，綿亙山谷且三千里，分軍屯守，烽堠相望。

translations.literal: He restored Qin’s long-wall barrier; from Wencheng reaching to Jieshi, stretching through mountains and valleys nearly three thousand *li*, he divided armies to garrison and hold; beacon mounds faced one another in sight.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt the Qin line of wall from Wencheng to Jieshi, nearly three thousand *li* through hill country, with garrisons and beacons linked along its length.

sentences.zh: 由是邊境獲安，無犬吠之警，自漢魏征鎮莫之比焉。

translations.literal: By this the borderlands obtained peace; there was no dog-barking alarm; from Han and Wei expedition commands none matched it.
translations.idiomatic: The border knew such calm that dogs seldom barked at alarm—no frontier command since Han and Wei had matched it.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑諸種畏懼，遂殺大莫廆。

translations.literal: The Xianbei various kinds feared; thereupon they killed Damowei.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei, cowed by him, turned on Damowei and slew him.

sentences.zh: 彬欲討之，恐列上俟報，虜必逃散，乃發幽冀車牛。

translations.literal: Bin wished to punish them; he feared if he listed it above and awaited reply, the barbarians would certainly scatter and flee; thereupon he issued You and Ji carts and oxen.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Bin meant to strike them but knew a memorial and wait for approval would let the tribes scatter, so he requisitioned transport oxen from You and Ji without prior clearance.

sentences.zh: 參軍許祗密奏之。

translations.literal: Army adviser Xu Zhi secretly memorialized it.
translations.idiomatic: His adviser Xu Zhi reported this secretly to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔遣御史檻車征彬付廷尉，以事直見釋。

translations.literal: An edict sent the imperial secretary with a caged cart to summon Bin and deliver him to the commandant of justice; because the affair was straight he was released.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent a censor to haul him to the capital in a prison cart, but the commandant of justice cleared him as acting within right.

sentences.zh: 百姓追慕彬功德，生為立碑作頌。

translations.literal: The hundred surnames pursued and admired Bin’s merit and virtue; while living they for him set up a stele and made praise.
translations.idiomatic: The people, grateful for his rule, erected a monument and composed a eulogy while he still lived.

sentences.zh: 彬初受學于東海閻德，門徒甚多，獨目彬有廊廟才。

translations.literal: Bin at first received learning from Yan De of Donghai; disciples were very many; alone he eyed Bin as having hall-and-temple talent.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Bin had studied under Yan De of Donghai amid a large school; alone Yan marked him as material for high office.

sentences.zh: 及彬官成，而德已卒，乃為之立碑。

translations.literal: When Bin’s office was accomplished, De had already died; thereupon he for him set up a stele.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Tang Bin’s career flourished, Yan De was dead; Tang therefore raised a stele in his honor.

sentences.zh: 元康初，拜使持節、前將軍、領西戎校尉、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuankang, he was appointed credential bearer, general of the van, concurrent colonel of the western Rong, Yongzhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuankang he became credential bearer, General of the Van, concurrent Colonel of the Western Rong, and inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 下教曰：「此州名都，士人林藪。

translations.literal: He issued instruction, saying: “This province is a famous capital; gentry men are forest and marsh.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed, “Yongzhou is a renowned seat; its scholars gather like trees in a grove.”

sentences.zh: 處士皇甫申叔、嚴舒龍、姜茂時、梁子遠等，並志節清妙，履行高潔。

translations.literal: Recluses Huangfu Shenshen, Yan Shulong, Jiang Maoshi, Liang Ziyuan and others together had intent and integrity clear and subtle, conduct and practice lofty and pure.
translations.idiomatic: The recluses Huangfu Shenshen, Yan Shulong, Jiang Maoshi, and Liang Ziyuan combine sterling principle with spotless lives.”

sentences.zh: 踐境望風，虛心饑渴，思加延致，待以不臣之典。

translations.literal: Treading the territory and gazing at the wind, I am empty-hearted and hunger-thirst; I think to add summoning and bringing, treating them with the canon of not treating as subjects.
translations.idiomatic: I have long admired them and wish to invite them with the etiquette reserved for guests, not subjects.”

sentences.zh: 幅巾相見，論道而已，豈以吏職，屈染高規。

translations.literal: With headcloth we meet; we discuss the Way—that is all—how could with clerk duties I bend and stain lofty norms.
translations.idiomatic: We shall meet informally and speak of principle; I would not demean their high standard with petty bureaucratic demands.”

sentences.zh: 郡國備禮發遣，以副於邑之望。

translations.literal: Commanderies and kingdoms shall complete ritual and dispatch them, to match the prefecture-city’s hope.
translations.idiomatic: Let each district prepare proper escort and send them forward, as the capital expects.”

sentences.zh: 」於是四人皆到，彬敬而待之。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon the four men all arrived; Bin respected and treated them.
translations.idiomatic: ” All four came; Tang Bin received them with respect.

sentences.zh: 卒官，時年六十，諡曰襄，賜絹二百匹，錢二十萬。

translations.literal: He died in office; at the time his years were sixty; his posthumous title was Xiang; two hundred bolts of silk and two hundred thousand cash were granted.
translations.idiomatic: He died in post at sixty, posthumously titled Xiang, with two hundred bolts of silk and two hundred thousand cash granted for his funeral.

sentences.zh: 長子嗣，官至廣陵太守。

translations.literal: The eldest son succeeded; office reached Guangling grand administrator.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son succeeded him and rose to grand administrator of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 少子岐，征虜司馬。

translations.literal: The younger son Qi, General Who Conquers the Barbarians’ major.
translations.idiomatic: His younger son Tang Qi became a major on the staff of the General Who Conquers the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Shiping
translations.idiomatic: Shiping

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：孫氏負江山之阻隔，恃牛鬥之妖氛，奄有水鄉，抗衡上國。

translations.literal: The historians say: The Sun clan bore river-and-mountain’s blocking separation, relied on Ox-and-Dipper’s unlucky miasma, suddenly possessed the water country, and resisted the superior state.
translations.idiomatic: The historians remark: The Sun house leaned on the Yangtze’s barrier and the dire omens over the Wu stars, seized the lake country, and defied the central court.

sentences.zh: 二王屬當戎旅，受律遄征，渾既獻捷橫江，濬亦克清建鄴。

translations.literal: The two Wangs attached to the moment of armies, received the baton and swiftly campaigned; Hun already presented victory at Hengjiang; Jun also conquered and cleared Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: The two Wangs took the field under orders: Wang Hun won at Hengjiang, Wang Jun swept Jianye.

sentences.zh: 于時討吳之役，將帥雖多，定吳之功，此焉為最。

translations.literal: At that time in the campaign of punishing Wu, though generals and commanders were many, the merit of settling Wu, here was the foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Among the many commanders in the Wu expedition, theirs was the decisive share in finishing the war.

sentences.zh: 向使弘范父之不伐，慕陽夏之推功，上稟廟堂，下憑將士。

translations.literal: If only they had enlarged Fan-father’s not boasting, emulated Yangxia’s pushing merit, above reported to the temple hall, below relied on generals and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Had they honored Fan Wenzi’s habit of disclaiming merit and the Yangxia gentry’s willingness to yield credit, informing the high ministers above and trusting the commanders and troops below,

sentences.zh: 豈非茂勳茂德，善始善終者歟！

translations.literal: Would it not be luxuriant merit luxuriant virtue, those who begin well and end well!
translations.idiomatic: would they not have paired brilliant achievement with lasting virtue and matched a worthy end to a worthy beginning?

sentences.zh: 此而不存，彼焉是務。

translations.literal: This they did not preserve; that is what they strove for.
translations.idiomatic: Instead they abandoned that path and chased lesser quarrels.

sentences.zh: 或矜功負氣，或恃勢驕陵，競構南箕，成茲貝錦。

translations.literal: Some boasted merit and bore pride; some relied on power and acted arrogant; vying they framed Southern Dipper, completed this shell-brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Some swaggered over their feats, others threw their weight about; together they wove slanders like the “Southern Dipper” ode and the “shell-patterned brocade” calumny.

sentences.zh: 遂乃喧黷宸扆，斁亂彝倫，既為戒于功臣，亦致譏於清論，豈不惜哉！

translations.literal: Thereupon they clamored and defiled the imperial seat, disrupted and disordered constant norms; already they became a warning to meritorious ministers, also incurred ridicule in pure opinion—how not regrettable!
translations.idiomatic: They fouled the throne with wrangling, broke orderly relations, warned future generals against pride, and earned the censure of every fair judge—a pity indeed.

sentences.zh: 王濟遂驕父之褊心，乖爭子之明義，俊材雖多，亦奚以為也。

translations.literal: Wang Ji then was arrogant at father’s narrow heart, contrary to disputing son’s clear right—outstanding talent though many, what use also!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji aped his father’s pettiness and abandoned the decency a son owes—talent avails little without character.

sentences.zh: 唐彬畏避交爭，屬疾遲留，退讓之風，賢於渾濬遠矣。

translations.literal: Tang Bin feared and avoided cross quarrels, attached illness and delayed; retiring yielding wind—worthier than Hun and Jun by far.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Bin shunned the quarrel, lingered on pretext of illness, and showed a humility that puts Wang Hun and Wang Jun to shame.

sentences.zh: 傳云「不拘行檢」，安得長者之行哉！

translations.literal: The biography says “not constrained by conduct inspection”—how could that obtain an elder’s conduct!
translations.idiomatic: Yet the text calls him “unconcerned with propriety”—that is hardly the mark of a true gentleman.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：二王總戎，淮海攸同。

translations.literal: The praise says: The two Wangs commanded armies; Huai and sea together.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium runs: “Two Wangs held the hosts; Huai and sea bowed as one.”

sentences.zh: 渾既害善，濬亦矜功。

translations.literal: Hun already harmed the good; Jun also boasted merit.
translations.idiomatic: Hun injured the worthy; Jun preened over his deeds.

sentences.zh: 武子豪桀，夙參朝列。

translations.literal: Wuzi was a heroic outstanding man; early he joined the court ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji, a swaggering blade, long sat in court.

sentences.zh: 逞欲牛心，紆情馬埒。

translations.literal: He vented desire at Ox-heart, wound sentiment at horse levee.
translations.idiomatic: He chased rare dishes and poured passion into the polo bank.

sentences.zh: 儒宗知退，避名全節。

translations.literal: The Confucian exemplar knew retiring; avoiding name he preserved integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Bin, the gentleman who knew retreat, shunned fame and kept his honor whole.
